issue.title: [BUG] [Pieces] Google Gemini model dropdown hides every Gemini 3+ text model (hard-coded prefix whitelist)
issue.body:
## Problem

Model dropdown on Generate Content, Chat, Count Tokens, Generate Content from Image, File Search lists only Gemini 2.5 Flash / Pro / Flash-Lite as text models. No Gemini 3.x or 4 text model is offered. Typing the model name as a custom value works.

Piece 0.5.3 (current npm) and main behave the same.

Ref: Pylon 6973

## Root cause

`packages/pieces/community/google-gemini/src/lib/common/common.ts:12-24`: the dropdown calls `ListModels` live, then keeps only names matching a hard-coded prefix list:

```ts
export const allowedLLMs = [
  'gemini-1.5-flash', 'gemini-1.5-flash-8b', 'gemini-1.5-pro',
  'gemini-2.0-flash', 'gemini-2.0-flash-lite',
  'gemini-2.5-flash', 'gemini-2.5-pro',
  'gemini-3-pro'
];
const isAllowedLLM = (model) => allowedLLMs.some((a) => model.name.startsWith(`models/${a}`));
```

Last edited 2025-11-20 (c75bbf73834). Google shut down `gemini-3-pro-preview`, so `gemini-3-pro` now matches only the Nano Banana image models.

Live `ListModels` (2026-11-10, 61 models) through this filter:

* shown: gemini-2.5-flash, gemini-2.5-pro, gemini-2.5-flash-lite, 2.5 TTS / native-audio variants, gemini-2.5-flash-image, gemini-3-pro-image(-preview)
* hidden: gemini-3-flash-preview, gemini-3.1-pro-preview, gemini-3.1-flash-lite, gemini-3.5-flash, gemini-3.5-flash-lite, gemini-3.6-flash, gemini-3.7-flash, gemini-3.8-flash, gemini-4-argon

Google deprecates 2.5 Flash and 2.5 Pro on 2026-12-01, after which the text dropdown is near empty.

## Fix

Replace the whitelist with a capability filter so new releases appear automatically:

* keep models whose `supportedGenerationMethods` includes `generateContent`
* exclude the existing `isTtsModel` / `isImageModel` / `isVeoModel` / `isEmbeddingModel` matches, plus `live`, `transcribe`, `robotics`, `omni`, `gemma`
* bump `defaultLLM` off `gemini-1.5-flash` (no longer returned by the API)

Ships as a piece bump, no platform release needed.

issue.title: [BUG] Step output copy buttons toast "Copied to clipboard" even when the clipboard write is rejected
issue.body:
## Problem

Copy buttons on step output / data panels call `navigator.clipboard.writeText()` without awaiting it and always toast "Copied to clipboard". When the write rejects (`NotAllowedError: The Clipboard API has been blocked because of a permissions policy`, e.g. builder embedded in an iframe whose parent frame lacks `allow="clipboard-write"`), the user sees a success toast while the clipboard stays empty. Only the webhook URL / markdown code-block copy reports the failure.

Ref: Pylon 6422

Reported by an embed customer. Their actual cause was a missing `allow` attribute on their own outer iframe; the false success toast hid it for months.

## Root cause

Fire-and-forget `writeText`, no `.catch`, unconditional success toast:

* `packages/web/src/app/builder/data-display/data-display-tabs.tsx:34`
* `packages/web/src/components/custom/json-viewer.tsx:55`
* `packages/web/src/components/custom/simple-json-viewer.tsx:33`

Same pattern elsewhere in `packages/web` (automations table URL copy, canvas context-menu "copy reference", invite dialog, chat message copy); same fix applies.

## Fix

Route these through the existing `useCopyToClipboard()` (`packages/web/src/components/custom/clipboard/use-copy-to-clipboard.ts`): it awaits `writeText`, toasts "Failed to copy to clipboard" on rejection and exposes `isCopied` for the check icon. Remove the unconditional `toast.success` calls.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Chrome. Embed the builder via the SDK inside a page that is itself a cross-origin iframe without `allow="clipboard-read; clipboard-write"`.
2. Open any step's output panel, click Copy.
3. Toast "Copied to clipboard"; clipboard unchanged; console shows `NotAllowedError ... permissions policy`.

issue.title: [BUG] Sync webhooks silently time out when trigger and response action are in different piece packages (isSamePiece gate)
issue.body:
## Summary

Synchronous webhook responses (`/api/v1/webhooks/{flowId}/sync`) silently time out at the internal `engineWatcher` 30s timeout when the action that calls `context.run.stop({ response })` is in a **different piece package** than the trigger. There is no error, log, or warning — the engine completes successfully (`status: OK`), but `engineWatcher#listen Timeout reached` fires and AP returns `204 No Content`.

The root cause is a hard gate in [`piece-executor.ts:165`](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/blob/main/packages/server/engine/src/lib/handler/piece-executor.ts) (verified on AP CE 0.81.0):

```ts
const isSamePiece = constants.triggerPieceName === action.settings.pieceName
if (!isNil(webhookResponse) && !isNil(constants.serverHandlerId) && !isNil(constants.httpRequestId) && isSamePiece) {
    await workerSocket.getWorkerClient().sendFlowResponse({...})
}
```

`sendFlowResponse` is only fired when `isSamePiece` is true. When it's false, the response signal is silently swallowed.

## Why this matters for piece authors

The piece-authoring docs and SDK types ([context.d.ts `RunContext.stop` / `RunContext.respond`](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/blob/main/packages/pieces/community/framework/src/lib/context.ts)) suggest that any action can emit a synchronous webhook response by calling `run.stop({ response })`. There is no documented constraint that the action must be in the same npm package as the trigger.

For an author building a custom workflow primitive split across two pieces — e.g., a typed input piece and a typed output piece — this gate is invisible:
- The action's `run.stop()` call appears to succeed
- The flow completes normally with `status: OK`
- The job log shows `Sandbox installation complete` and `Job completed by worker`
- But the `/sync` endpoint returns `204` after exactly 30s

The first AP issue you'd suspect is your own piece's code. Time spent diagnosing in our case: several hours, eventually resolved by reading the engine source on the running instance.

## Reproduction

1. Create two custom piece packages, A and B, both implementing the standard piece-framework v0.10+ API.
2. In A, define a `WEBHOOK` trigger.
3. In B, define an action whose `run` calls `context.run.stop({ response: { status: 200, body: { ok: true }, headers: {} } })`.
4. Build a flow: trigger from A → (any middle steps) → action from B as the last step. Publish.
5. POST to `${AP_URL}/api/v1/webhooks/${flowId}/sync`.
6. Observe: response arrives after 30s as 204 with empty body. AP logs show `engineWatcher#listen Timeout reached`. The flow's job log shows `status: OK`.

For comparison, putting the same trigger + action in **a single piece package** (i.e. one `createPiece({ triggers: [...], actions: [...] })`) makes `isSamePiece` true and the response is delivered in milliseconds.

## Suggested fixes (in order of preference)

1. **Document the constraint.** Add to the synchronous-webhook docs that the action calling `run.stop`/`run.respond` must reside in the same piece as the trigger. This alone would prevent the diagnostic dead-end.

2. **Surface a runtime warning.** In `piece-executor.ts`, when `isSamePiece` is false but `webhookResponse` is set, log a warning explaining why the response was dropped, e.g.:
   ```
   [piece-executor] run.stop response ignored: action piece '${action.settings.pieceName}' does not match trigger piece '${constants.triggerPieceName}'. The synchronous webhook response is only forwarded when both are in the same piece. See docs/sync-webhook-constraints.
   ```

3. **(Stretch) lift the gate.** If there's no architectural reason to require `isSamePiece`, allow any action's `run.stop` to forward the response, regardless of package. This would enable composable workflow primitives split across multiple pieces.

## Environment

- AP version: `0.81.0`, edition `ce`
- Pieces framework: `@activepieces/pieces-framework@0.10.x`
- Self-hosted via the standard `activepieces/activepieces:latest` Docker image

## Related context

We documented our diagnostic journey in our internal plan doc — happy to share more detail if useful.

issue.title: Document KEDA-based autoscaling using /v1/worker-machines/queue-metrics
issue.body:
Reference manifests for queue-depth autoscaling of Activepieces on Kubernetes via KEDA, using the existing platform-admin endpoint `GET /api/v1/worker-machines/queue-metrics`.

## 6. KEDA resources

### 6.1 Secret

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: ap-keda-auth
  namespace: activepieces
type: Opaque
stringData:
  apiKey: "sk-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"
```

### 6.2 TriggerAuthentication

```yaml
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: TriggerAuthentication
metadata:
  name: ap-queue-metrics-auth
  namespace: activepieces
spec:
  secretTargetRef:
    - parameter: token
      name: ap-keda-auth
      key: apiKey
```

`parameter: token` + `authMode: bearer` makes KEDA send `Authorization: Bearer sk-…` on every poll.

### 6.3 ScaledObject — single queue

```yaml
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:
  name: activepieces-worker
  namespace: activepieces
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    name: activepieces                    # Deployment name
  pollingInterval: 15                     # seconds between polls
  cooldownPeriod: 180                     # seconds idle before scaling to min
  minReplicaCount: 2
  maxReplicaCount: 30
  fallback:
    failureThreshold: 3
    replicas: 5                           # if endpoint fails 3x, hold at 5
  advanced:
    horizontalPodAutoscalerConfig:
      behavior:
        scaleUp:
          stabilizationWindowSeconds: 0   # scale up immediately
          policies:
            - type: Percent
              value: 100                  # double pods…
              periodSeconds: 30
            - type: Pods
              value: 4                    # …or +4 pods, whichever larger
              periodSeconds: 30
          selectPolicy: Max
        scaleDown:
          stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300 # 5 min smoothing
          policies:
            - type: Percent
              value: 25
              periodSeconds: 60
  triggers:
    - type: metrics-api
      metadata:
        targetValue: "50"                 # waiting jobs per pod
        url: "http://activepieces.activepieces.svc.cluster.local/api/v1/worker-machines/queue-metrics"
        valueLocation: 'queues.#(name=="workerJobs").waiting'
        authMode: "bearer"
      authenticationRef:
        name: ap-queue-metrics-auth
```

issue.title: [BUG]: "Generate Sample Data" silently fails when there are no recent event
issue.body: **Describe the bug** When a polling-style trigger's test function succeeds but returns zero events, the **Generate Sample Data** / **Load Sample Data** button silently does nothing, no error, no message, no state change. To the user it looks as if the click never registered. This adds confusion to the users. A reproducible scenario: connecting a freshly-created Telegram bot whose token is valid but who has not yet received any messages. The bot's `test()` hook calls Telegram's `getUpdates?offset=-5`, which legitimately returns an empty list, and the UI provides no feedback about this outcome. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Create a new project in Activepieces. 2. Create a new flow and add the **Telegram Bot → New message** trigger. 3. Create a fresh Telegram bot via BotFather and connect it (valid token), without sending any message to the bot first. 4. Click **Generate Sample Data**. 5. Observe in DevTools: `POST /api/v1/test-trigger` returns HTTP 200 with `{ "next": null, "previous": null, "data": [] }`. The UI shows no feedback — same state as before the click. **Expected behavior** The user should be told that no recent events were found and given guidance on how to produce one. for example, an inline notice indicating that no data was found in the connected piece, asking them to perform an action there before retesting. **Screenshots** **Additional context** N/A

issue.title: [BUG]: docs incorrectly suggest setting `AP_DEV_PIECES` via inline shell prefix
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
The development setup docs at [`docs/build-pieces/building-pieces/development-setup.mdx`](https://www.activepieces.com/docs/build-pieces/building-pieces/development-setup#pieces-development) instruct contributors to set `AP_DEV_PIECES` via an inline shell prefix:

```sh
AP_DEV_PIECES=google-sheets,cal-com npm start
```

In practice this does not take effect for the running dev servers. Turborepo's `serve` task does not forward shell-set environment variables to its spawned `api` / `worker` tasks, so the dev servers only see the value configured in `.env.dev`. Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Clone the repo and run `node tools/setup-dev.js` once.
2. Edit `.env.dev` so `AP_DEV_PIECES=cal-com`.
3. Try to override via shell: `AP_DEV_PIECES=google-sheets npm start`.
4. Observe that the dev server still loads `cal-com`, not `google-sheets`.

**Expected behavior**
The docs should make it clear that `AP_DEV_PIECES` (and similar dev env vars like `AP_PIECES_SYNC_MODE`) must be set inside `.env.dev`, and that inline shell prefixes do not propagate to the dev servers.

**Screenshots**
N/A

**Additional context**
- The build-time step (`tools/setup-dev.js`) *does* respect shell-set values because it reads `process.env.AP_DEV_PIECES || envConfig.AP_DEV_PIECES`. This is partly why the issue is easy to miss, the build picks up the shell value, but the running dev servers don't.

issue.title: Document KEDA-based autoscaling using /v1/worker-machines/queue-metrics
issue.body:
Reference manifests for queue-depth autoscaling of Activepieces on Kubernetes via KEDA, using the existing platform-admin endpoint `GET /api/v1/worker-machines/queue-metrics`.

## 6. KEDA resources

### 6.1 Secret

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: ap-keda-auth
  namespace: activepieces
type: Opaque
stringData:
  apiKey: "sk-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"
```

### 6.2 TriggerAuthentication

```yaml
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: TriggerAuthentication
metadata:
  name: ap-queue-metrics-auth
  namespace: activepieces
spec:
  secretTargetRef:
    - parameter: token
      name: ap-keda-auth
      key: apiKey
```

`parameter: token` + `authMode: bearer` makes KEDA send `Authorization: Bearer sk-…` on every poll.

### 6.3 ScaledObject — single queue

```yaml
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:
  name: activepieces-worker
  namespace: activepieces
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    name: activepieces                    # Deployment name
  pollingInterval: 15                     # seconds between polls
  cooldownPeriod: 180                     # seconds idle before scaling to min
  minReplicaCount: 2
  maxReplicaCount: 30
  fallback:
    failureThreshold: 3
    replicas: 5                           # if endpoint fails 3x, hold at 5
  advanced:
    horizontalPodAutoscalerConfig:
      behavior:
        scaleUp:
          stabilizationWindowSeconds: 0   # scale up immediately
          policies:
            - type: Percent
              value: 100                  # double pods…
              periodSeconds: 30
            - type: Pods
              value: 4                    # …or +4 pods, whichever larger
              periodSeconds: 30
          selectPolicy: Max
        scaleDown:
          stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300 # 5 min smoothing
          policies:
            - type: Percent
              value: 25
              periodSeconds: 60
  triggers:
    - type: metrics-api
      metadata:
        targetValue: "50"                 # waiting jobs per pod
        url: "http://activepieces.activepieces.svc.cluster.local/api/v1/worker-machines/queue-metrics"
        valueLocation: 'queues.#(name=="workerJobs").waiting'
        authMode: "bearer"
      authenticationRef:
        name: ap-queue-metrics-auth
```

issue.title: bug: Invited platform admins can modify/deactivate   the platform owner and other admins
issue.body:
Invited platform administrators (`PlatformRole.ADMIN`) are currently able to modify (change role/status) or
delete the platform owner and peer administrators through the platform user management endpoints.

 An administrator should not have permission to:
    1. Deactivate, demote, or delete the platform owner.
    2. Modify or delete other administrators.
    3. Deactivate, demote, or delete their own account (to prevent lockouts).

### Steps to reproduce
   1. Log in as the Platform Owner.
   2. Invite a new user with the `Admin` role.
   3. Log in as the invited `Admin`.
   4. Go to the Users management table.
   5. Click the action menu next to the Platform Owner or another Admin.
   6. Change their role (e.g., demote the owner to `Member`) or deactivate/delete their account.		

### Expected behavior
 Only the Platform Owner should be authorized to modify or delete other administrators. Invited
  administrators should be restricted from altering the platform owner, other admins, or themselves.

#### Fixed in pr = https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/pull/14085

issue.title: [BUG] Chrome "password found in a data breach" popup on connection and platform secret fields
issue.body:
## Problem

Chrome breach-checks every `type="password"` field at form submit; API keys / client secrets matching Google's breach DB trigger the native "password found in a data breach" popup, and Chrome offers to save them to the password manager. Same defect as activepieces/activepieces#14194 (variable dialog, fixed in PR 14198). Still present on 7 secret fields inside submitted forms:

* `packages/web/src/app/connections/secret-text-connection-settings.tsx:38` (SecretInput)
* `packages/web/src/app/connections/basic-secret-connection-settings.tsx:56` (SecretInput)
* `packages/web/src/app/connections/oauth2-connection-settings.tsx:131` (SecretInput)
* `packages/web/src/app/builder/piece-properties/properties-utils.tsx:263` (SECRET_TEXT props)
* `packages/web/src/app/routes/platform/setup/ai-capabilities/ai-capability-dialog.tsx:173` (apiKey)
* `packages/web/src/app/routes/platform/setup/pieces/update-oauth2-dialog.tsx:146` (clientSecret)
* `packages/web/src/app/routes/platform/setup/ai/universal-pieces/upsert-provider-config-form.tsx:308` (AWS secretAccessKey)

The connection dialog is the highest-traffic secret-entry surface, so it triggers the popup more often than the variable dialog ever did.

## Root cause

Rows 1-4 route through `packages/web/src/app/connections/secret-input.tsx` (single choke point passing `type="password"` through). Rows 5-7 are standalone inputs.

## Fix

Apply the PR 14198 pattern: `type="text"` + `cn(..., '[-webkit-text-security:disc]')` + `autoComplete="off"` + `spellCheck={false}`. Flip `SecretInput`'s inner Input once (fixes rows 1-4); patch the 3 platform dialogs individually.

## Out of scope

Sign-in / sign-up / change-password fields are real passwords and keep `type="password"`.

issue.title: CI hardening: PR branch name interpolated into ssh/git shell commands (script-injection risk)
issue.body:
### Summary

A few `pull_request`-triggered workflows interpolate the PR branch name
(`github.head_ref` / `github.event.pull_request.head.ref`) **directly into `ssh` and `git` shell
commands**. A branch name can contain shell metacharacters (git allows `;`, `$()`, backticks, `|`, …),
so a crafted branch name could inject commands into the runner — and, in `remove-environment.yml` /
`setup-environment.yml`, into the `ssh preview-server` remote shell. Raising it as a hardening note.

### The interpolation points (observation)

- [`remove-environment.yml`](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/blob/3fa6a2c58b818944a816b7df732244408f4310f1/.github/workflows/remove-environment.yml) (`on: pull_request: [closed]`):
  ```
  ssh preview-server -t -t 'bash -ic "… node dist/index.js remove ${{ github.head_ref }}; exit"'
  ```
- [`setup-environment.yml`](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/blob/3fa6a2c58b818944a816b7df732244408f4310f1/.github/workflows/setup-environment.yml) (`on: pull_request`):
  ```
  BRANCH=${{ github.head_ref || github.ref_name }}
  ssh preview-server … "… node dist/index.js setup ${BRANCH}; exit"
  ```
- [`crowdin-pr-merger.yml`](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/blob/3fa6a2c58b818944a816b7df732244408f4310f1/.github/workflows/crowdin-pr-merger.yml) (`on: pull_request`):
  ```
  git fetch origin ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}:${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}
  git reset --hard origin/${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}
  git push  origin HEAD:${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}
  ```

### Suggested mitigation

Per GitHub's [script-injection guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#understanding-the-risk-of-script-injections),
pass the ref through an `env:` variable and quote it in the shell, e.g.:

```yaml
env:
  HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}
run: |
  git fetch origin "$HEAD_REF:$HEAD_REF"
  git reset --hard "origin/$HEAD_REF"
```

For the `ssh …` cases, pass `HEAD_REF` through and quote it inside the remote command (or validate it
against `^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$` first), since the value crosses into a second shell.

Happy to open a PR for the `git`/`BRANCH` ones; the `ssh` remote-quoting is environment-specific, so I
wanted to check the approach with you first. Thanks for Activepieces!

<sub>AI-assisted; I verified the workflows and triggers myself against commit `3fa6a2c58b81`.</sub>

issue.title: Vulnerable dependencies reported by Trivy
issue.body:
## Issue title

**Update vulnerable dependencies reported by Trivy: 6 Critical and 61 High SCA findings**

### Summary

A Trivy Software Composition Analysis scan of Activepieces identified **67 Critical and High severity findings** in the project dependency tree:

- **6 Critical findings**
- **61 High findings**
- **62 vulnerability records**
- **5 license-policy findings**
- **52 unique vulnerability or license identifiers**
- **26 affected packages**

The scan was performed against Activepieces version `0.86.2`, commit `36ba96ba11`, using the Bun package manager.

Some of the reported issues may allow arbitrary code execution, path traversal, arbitrary file read or write, denial of service, cross-site scripting, prototype pollution, credential disclosure, request manipulation, or cryptographic key extraction.

Please update the affected dependency constraints in the relevant `package.json` files and regenerate `bun.lock` so that both direct and transitive dependencies resolve to patched versions.

No attempt was made to exploit these vulnerabilities against a running Activepieces instance. The findings are based on dependency versions detected by Trivy, and the practical exploitability of each vulnerability depends on whether the affected functionality is reachable in Activepieces.

- **Analysis type:** `SCA`

issue.title: [BUG]: Azure OpenAI image deployments are always classified as TEXT
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**

`packages/server/api/src/app/ai/providers/azure-provider.ts:33` types every Azure deployment as `AIProviderModelType.TEXT` unconditionally. Azure OpenAI can host image deployments (`gpt-image-*`, `dall-e-*`), so those deployments never appear in `AI → Generate Image` and instead appear in the Ask AI model dropdown, where they fail at runtime.

Same user-visible symptom as [GIT-1678](<https://linear.app/activepieces/issue/GIT-1678>), different provider.

**Why it needs a different fix from** activepieces/activepieces#14475

activepieces/activepieces#14475 was fixed for OpenAI with a name test (`gpt-image` prefix plus the two dall-e ids). That approach does not transfer: **Azure deployment names are chosen by the customer**, so a deployment serving `gpt-image-2` can be named `my-images` or anything else. A prefix or substring test on the deployment name is unreliable in both directions.

Options worth weighing:

* Read the deployment's underlying model from the Azure management/deployments API rather than inferring from the name.
* Let the admin declare the modality per deployment in Platform Settings, as `CUSTOM` and `CLOUDFLARE_GATEWAY` already do (they carry a user-entered `modelType`).

**Expected behavior**

An Azure deployment backed by an image model is classified `IMAGE` and is selectable in Generate Image.

**Additional context**

Found during the activepieces/activepieces#14475 sibling sweep. For comparison, `google-provider.ts:23`, `openrouter-provider.ts:32`, and `bedrock-provider.ts` already classify correctly (OpenRouter and Bedrock use real modality data from the API).

issue.title: Worker RAM shows ~97% on idle hosts when containers have no memory limit
issue.body:
### Where

`packages/server/utils/src/system-usage.ts` — `getContainerMemoryUsage()`

### What happens

When containers run without a memory limit, both the cgroup and `constrainedMemory()` branches are skipped and it falls back to `si.mem()`, reporting `mem.used / mem.total`. `mem.used` is `total - free`, which counts page cache.

`getCgroupMemory()` already subtracts `inactive_file` for exactly this reason, so the host fallback is inconsistent with the branch above it.

issue.title: [BUG] Event Streaming: cross-action handler-flow loop survives the cycle guard — needs a dispatch hop counter, not URL matching
issue.body:
## Problem

The cycle guard in `skipInternalDestinationsOnFlowCycle` (`packages/server/api/src/app/event-destinations/event-destinations.service.ts`) fires only when some destination in the *current event's* candidate list targets the flow that emitted that event. Two flows wired to each other via **different** event actions never satisfy that, so the loop is unbounded:

* D1: url → `/v1/webhooks/<Y>`, events `[FLOW_RUN_STARTED]`
* D2: url → `/v1/webhooks/<X>`, events `[FLOW_RUN_FINISHED]`

X starts → event(STARTED, flowId=X) → candidates = `[D1]` only (D2 isn't subscribed to STARTED) → D1 targets Y ≠ X → guard skips → Y runs. Y finishes → event(FINISHED, flowId=Y) → candidates = `[D2]` → D2 targets X ≠ Y → guard skips → X runs → X starts → loop.

This is pre-existing and was explicitly disclosed as out of scope in #14293 (activepieces/activepieces#14290), which fixed the *same-action* case for non-`AP_FRONTEND_URL` hosts. Confirmed by reading the merged guard, not reproduced live.

## Why URL matching can't fix it

activepieces/activepieces#14290 was the **second** time this guard failed open on a URL-shape assumption — first `destination.origin === getPublicApiUrl().origin`, then the `/v1/webhooks/<flowId>` path marker. Each fix narrows the shape it recognizes; neither bounds the *chain*. The guard is also now spread across three parsers with different semantics (`matchInternalWebhookFlowId` origin-strict and non-decoding, `extractWebhookFlowIdCandidate` host-agnostic and decoding, `webhookRouteSuffix`), which is where the next divergence will come from.

## Proposed fix

Bound the dispatch chain instead of pattern-matching URLs: carry a hop/depth counter (or an originating-event id + visited-flow set) on the event → `EVENT_DESTINATION` job → synthesized webhook payload → the resulting run's emitted events, and drop dispatch past a small limit. Host-, path- and encoding-independent, and it closes the same-action case as a side effect.

Worth pairing with: collapse the three URL parsers so `matchInternalWebhookFlowId` does the origin check and then delegates to `extractWebhookFlowIdCandidate`, making divergence structurally impossible.

## Impact

Same blast radius as activepieces/activepieces#14290 — a queue flood from one webhook POST (838 runs in ~3 min was measured there, Pylon 5378) — but reachable only with the cross-action wiring above, so lower likelihood. No customer report for this variant yet.

## Notes

* Guard semantics, the collateral-drop behaviour, and this open hole are documented in `brain/wiki/eventing-webhooks/event-destinations.md`.

issue.title: [BUG] Bare date literals in date-typed formula args are evaluated as arithmetic — get_year(2025-01-15) returns 2009
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**

The formula evaluator's implicit-quoting pass only quotes bare literals in `string`-typed argument positions. `date`-typed positions are skipped, so a bare date literal like `2025-01-15` is handed to `expr-eval`, which happily parses it as the arithmetic expression `2025 - 1 - 15` and returns `2009`. The result is a silently wrong date — no evaluator error, and no editor type error either.

This contradicts every example in the project's own reference table (`docs/flows/formula-reference.mdx`), which states "Quotes around text arguments are optional" and shows all Date examples with bare literals — and those same examples are rendered in-product by the function hover popover (`example` / `exampleResult` in `function-registry.ts`).

**To Reproduce**

In any text input that supports data manipulation, insert a date function with `/` and type a literal date into the date slot — exactly as `docs/flows/formula-reference.mdx` shows:

| Expression | `formula-reference.mdx` says | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| `get_year(2025-01-15)` | `2025` | `2009` |
| `get_day(2025-01-15)` | `15` | `1` |
| `get_day_of_week(2025-01-15)` | `Wednesday` | `Thursday` |
| `days_between(2025-01-01; 2025-01-15)` | `14` | `5113` |
| `is_before(2025-01-01; 2025-02-01)` | `TRUE` | `false` |
| `format_date(2025-01-15; "MMM DD, YYYY")` | `Jan 15, 2025` | `Jan 01, 2009` |
| `add_days(2025-01-15; 30)` | `Feb 14, 2025` | `2009-01-31T00:00:00.000Z` |
| `start_of_day(2025-01-15T14:30:00Z)` | `2025-01-15T00:00:00Z` | *step fails: "Could not evaluate this formula"* |
| `hours_between(2025-01-15T09:00:00Z; 2025-01-15T17:30:00Z)` | `8` | *step fails* |

21 of the 22 examples in the Date table do not match. (The one that "passes", `get_month`, is a coincidence: January in both 2009 and 2025.) The Text table, by contrast, matches.

Mixing a mention with a literal cut-off date — a very common pattern — silently flips a branch:

```
{{order.created}} = "2025-12-01"

days_between({{order.created}}; 2025-12-31)  →  16040   (should be 30)
is_before({{order.created}}; 2026-01-01)     →  false   (should be true)
```

`2026-01-01` becomes `2026 - 1 - 1 = 2024`, so the comparison is made against 2024-01-01. When this feeds an `if` / Router condition, records get routed down the wrong branch with no error anywhere.

Verified against `main` @ `8124c542` by driving `formulaEvaluator.evaluate()` directly (the same entry point `props-resolver.ts` uses at flow runtime), with the repo's own formula test suite (259 tests) passing in the same harness.

**Expected behavior**

Bare date literals in `date`-typed argument positions should be treated as date strings, matching both the reference docs and the in-builder hover examples — the same way bare literals in `string`-typed positions already are. `get_year(2025-01-15)` should return `2025`.

Two failure modes today, one root cause:

- Plain `YYYY-MM-DD` → parsed as subtraction → **silently wrong date** (`format_date`, `format_date_long`, `relative_time`, `add_days`, `subtract_days`, `days_between`, `get_day`, `get_month`, `get_year`, `get_day_of_week`, `start_of_month`, `end_of_month`, `is_before`, `is_after`).
- ISO 8601 with a time (contains `:`) → `expr-eval` parse error → **step fails at runtime** (`format_time`, `add_hours`, `add_minutes`, `hours_between`, `start_of_day`, `end_of_day`, `is_same_day`, `convert_timezone`).

**Screenshots**

Not applicable — evaluator-level bug; the tables above show the mismatch.

**Additional context**

Root cause is in `packages/core/formula/src/lib/formula-evaluator.ts:213-214`:

```ts
const expectedSpec = fn.argTypes[Math.min(i, fn.argTypes.length - 1)]
const shouldQuote = expectedSpec === 'string' ||
    (Array.isArray(expectedSpec) && (expectedSpec as string[]).includes('string'))
```

`'date'` is neither `'string'` nor an array, so `shouldQuote` is `false` and the bare literal reaches `expr-eval`.

An internal contradiction confirms it: `to_date` declares `argTypes: [['string', 'date']]` (`function-registry.ts:803`), so its union *does* contain `'string'`, it *is* quoted, and `to_date(2025-01-15)` returns the correct `2025-01-15T00:00:00.000Z`. Same literal, `get_year` gets it wrong.

The editor's static check doesn't catch it either: `inferArgType` bails out on any text matching `EXPRESSION_OPERATOR_REGEX` (`function-type-checker.ts:223`), and `2025-01-15` contains `-`. `typeCheckTiptapDoc` returns an empty error map for `get_year(2025-01-15)`, while correctly flagging `round_up(hello)`.

Suggested minimal fix — include `date` in the implicit-quoting whitelist:

```diff
             const expectedSpec = fn.argTypes[Math.min(i, fn.argTypes.length - 1)]
-            const shouldQuote = expectedSpec === 'string' ||
-                (Array.isArray(expectedSpec) && (expectedSpec as string[]).includes('string'))
+            const specs = Array.isArray(expectedSpec) ? expectedSpec : [expectedSpec]
+            const shouldQuote = specs.some((s) => s === 'string' || s === 'date')
             return shouldQuote ? quoteIfBare(inner) : inner
```

`quoteIfBare` already skips `__ap_` variable placeholders, already-quoted values and nested function calls, so `format_date({{trigger.date}}; ...)`, `add_days(now(); 5)` and `hours_between(start_of_day(now()); now())` are unaffected. I verified locally that with this patch every Date-table example becomes semantically correct and all 259 existing formula tests (`packages/core/shared/test/formula/*.test.ts`) still pass.

Why CI missed this: every date test in `function-evaluator.test.ts` hand-quotes its literals (e.g. `result('is_before("2024-01-01";"2024-02-01")')`), so the unquoted path — the one the docs and the in-builder hover popover tell users to write — is never exercised.

I have the fix plus regression tests ready on a fork branch. I read CONTRIBUTING.md and understand unsolicited external PRs are currently paused and auto-closed, so I'm not opening one — happy to submit it if maintainers want it (or feel free to just take the diff above).

*Disclosure: this report was prepared with AI assistance; the bug was reproduced locally and every claim above was verified against the code and re-checked by a human before filing.*

```diff
+            const specs = Array.isArray(expectedSpec) ? expectedSpec : [expectedSpec]
+            const shouldQuote = specs.some((s) => s === 'string' || s === 'date')
             return shouldQuote ? quoteIfBare(inner) : inner
```

`quoteIfBare` already skips `__ap_` variable placeholders, already-quoted values and nested function calls, so `format_date({{trigger.date}}; ...)`, `add_days(now(); 5)` and `hours_between(start_of_day(now()); now())` are unaffected. Why CI missed this: every date test in `function-evaluator.test.ts` hand-quotes its literals (e.g. `result('is_before("2024-01-01";"2024-02-01")')`), so the unquoted path — the one the docs and the in-builder hover popover tell users to write — is never exercised.

I have the fix plus regression tests ready on a fork branch. I read CONTRIBUTING.md and understand unsolicited external PRs are currently paused and auto-closed, so I'm not opening one — happy to submit it if maintainers want it (or feel free to just take the diff above).

*Disclosure: this report was prepared with AI assistance; the bug was reproduced locally and every claim above was verified against the code and re-checked by a human before filing.*

issue.title: [Connections] Changing a piece's auth type silently breaks existing connections
issue.body:
## Summary

When a piece changes its declared authentication method — most commonly moving from a single `PieceAuth.X()` to an array of methods — connections created under the old shape keep their original `value.type` in the database. Nothing in the platform notices the mismatch:

- the connection is not migrated,
- the type is not validated against the piece's current auth methods at read time,
- the status stays `ACTIVE` and the UI keeps showing the connection as connected,
- the piece receives a value shape it no longer expects and fails at runtime in a way that points the user at the wrong thing.

The user sees a green, "working" connection whose every API call fails. There is no signal anywhere that reconnecting is what's needed.

## Reproduction

SavvyCal, with a connection created before #12233 (merged 2026-05-06).

That PR changed the piece's auth from:

```ts
export const savvyCalAuth = PieceAuth.SecretText({ ... })
```

to:

```ts
export const savvyCalAuth = [PieceAuth.OAuth2({ ... }), PieceAuth.CustomAuth({ props: { token } })]
```

The pre-existing connection is stored as `{ type: 'SECRET_TEXT', secret_text: 'pt_secret_…' }`. The piece's token accessor is:

```ts
export function getToken(auth: SavvyCalAuthValue): string {
  if (auth.type === AppConnectionType.CUSTOM_AUTH) {
    return auth.props.token;
  }
  return auth.access_token;
}
```

`SECRET_TEXT` matches neither branch's intent, falls through to `auth.access_token`, and returns `undefined`. Every request goes out as `Authorization: Bearer undefined` and comes back `401 Unauthenticated` — including `/v1/me`, the endpoint the piece's own `validate` uses.

Observed behaviour:

- The connection shows **Active** on the Connections page and **Connected** in the flow builder.
- Every action fails with `401`, which reads as "your token expired" — the token was in fact valid the whole time.
- Dynamic dropdowns that catch their own errors show generic "failed to load" placeholders, hiding the 401 entirely.
- The only fix is to **delete and recreate** the connection. Editing it in place does not help, because the stored `type` is what's wrong.

Diagnosing this took several hours and required reading the piece's git history. Nothing in the product pointed at the cause.

## Root cause

Three things compound:

**1. No type compatibility check at read time.** `getConnectionValue` in `packages/server/engine/src/lib/piece-context/connection-resolver.ts` passes `connection.value` straight through to the piece. There is no comparison against the auth methods the piece currently declares.

**2. No migration path.** There is no migration code anywhere under `packages/server/api/src/app/app-connection/`. `validateConnectionValue` in `app-connection-service.ts` switches on the *incoming* value's type at creation time and never cross-checks it against the piece's declared auth. Once stored, a value's type is never revisited.

**3. The status can never flip.** `needRefresh` (`app-connection.handler.ts:267`) only handles the OAuth2 variants and `CUSTOM_AUTH`. `SECRET_TEXT` falls through to the default and never refreshes, so it never reaches the `catch` block that would set `AppConnectionStatus.ERROR`. A static-token connection stays `ACTIVE` permanently regardless of whether it works. The only live check in the product is the manual **Revalidate** button, which exists solely on the Connections page — not in the flow builder, where users actually hit the problem.

Worth noting: connections already store `pieceVersion`, so the information needed to detect a stale value shape is present today.

## Scope

The bug is one piece today, but nothing prevents the next one.

28 pieces currently declare multi-method auth. 18 of them migrated from a single `PieceAuth.X()` to an array after connections could already exist. 17 of those 18 kept their original method and added others alongside it (`OAuth2 → [OAuth2, …]`, `CustomAuth → [CustomAuth, …]`), so existing connections still match a declared type and keep working.

SavvyCal is the only one that dropped its original type: `SecretText → [OAuth2, CustomAuth]`. That is the breaking shape, and it went unnoticed for three months because the platform reports the broken connection as `ACTIVE`.

`fathom` and `mistral-ai` made the same `SecretText`-to-array move but still declare `SecretText`, so they are unaffected — which is luck, not a guard rail. Nothing in review, CI, or runtime distinguishes their case from SavvyCal's.

## Suggested direction

Roughly in order of value:

1. **Detect and surface the mismatch.** When resolving a connection, compare `connection.value.type` against the piece's currently declared auth methods. On mismatch, set the connection to `ERROR` with an explicit message — "this connection was created with an authentication method this piece no longer supports, please reconnect" — instead of handing the piece a shape it can't read.
2. **Make the builder's status reflect reality**, rather than a stored value that some connection types can never update.
3. **Optionally, an auth migration hook** so piece authors can map an old stored shape onto a new one instead of forcing every user to reconnect.
4. **Optionally, a CI check** that flags when a piece version removes an auth type that a previous version declared — this is a breaking change for existing connections and currently passes review unnoticed.

Even just (1) would have turned this from a multi-hour investigation into a one-line message.

## Environment

- Activepieces Cloud (`cloud.activepieces.com`)
- Piece: `@activepieces/piece-savvycal` v0.1.6
- Connection created before 2026-05-06

issue.title: Piece selector tab labels truncated (e.g. "Approvals" shows as "Appr...")
issue.body: ## Bug description In the flow builder's piece selector, tab labels get cut off with an ellipsis even though there is plenty of horizontal space available (e.g. "Approvals" renders as "Appr...", "AI & Agents" as "AI & Ag..."). Since the truncated text has no tooltip, there's no way for a user to discover what the tab actually is. ## Screenshots ## Steps to reproduce 1. Open the flow builder and add/edit an action step to open the piece selector. 2. Look at the tab row (Explore, AI & Agents, Apps, Utility, Approvals). 3. Labels wider than ~85px are ellipsized mid-word. ## Root cause This is a regression introduced in `8ccf91b2ad` ("feat: customizable piece selector (#13824)"). Before that PR, `packages/web/src/features/pieces/components/piece-selector-tabs.tsx` rendered the label as: ```tsx {tab.name} ``` with the `TabsTrigger` using `grow` inside a CSS grid (`gridTemplateColumns: repeat(tabs.length, minmax(0, 1fr))`) — long labels simply wrapped to a second line. PR #13824 switched the tab row to a flex layout with a fixed-width trigger (`w-[85px] max-w-[85px]`) and added `truncate w-full text-center` to the label span, which turns any label wider than 85px into a single-line ellipsis cutoff instead of wrapping. ## Expected behavior Tab labels should be fully readable — either by sizing the tab to its content (there's visibly spare width in the row) or, if truncation is still needed at narrow viewport widths, by wrapping the label in `TextWithTooltip` so the full name is discoverable on hover, per this repo's own convention for overflowing text. ## Suggested fix Give each `TabsTrigger` an auto/min-width instead of a fixed max-width, and drop `truncate` in favor of `whitespace-nowrap` so labels render on one line at their natural width.

issue.body:
## Summary

When a piece changes its declared authentication method — most commonly moving from a single `PieceAuth.X()` to an array of methods — connections created under the old shape keep their original `value.type` in the database. Nothing in the platform notices the mismatch:

- the connection is not migrated,
- the type is not validated against the piece's current auth methods at read time,
- the status stays `ACTIVE` and the UI keeps showing the connection as connected,
- the piece receives a value shape it no longer expects and fails at runtime in a way that points the user at the wrong thing.

The user sees a green, "working" connection whose every API call fails. There is no signal anywhere that reconnecting is what's needed.

## Reproduction

SavvyCal, with a connection created before #12233 (merged 2026-05-06).

That PR changed the piece's auth from:

```ts
export const savvyCalAuth = PieceAuth.SecretText({ ... })
```

to:

```ts
export const savvyCalAuth = [PieceAuth.OAuth2({ ... }), PieceAuth.CustomAuth({ props: { token } })]
```

The pre-existing connection is stored as `{ type: 'SECRET_TEXT', secret_text: 'pt_secret_…' }`. The piece's token accessor is:

```ts
export function getToken(auth: SavvyCalAuthValue): string {
  if (auth.type === AppConnectionType.CUSTOM_AUTH) {
    return auth.props.token;
  }
  return auth.access_token;
}
```

`SECRET_TEXT` matches neither branch's intent, falls through to `auth.access_token`, and returns `undefined`. Every request goes out as `Authorization: Bearer undefined` and comes back `401 Unauthenticated` — including `/v1/me`, the endpoint the piece's own `validate` uses.

Observed behaviour:

- The connection shows **Active** on the Connections page and **Connected** in the flow builder.
- Every action fails with `401`, which reads as "your token expired" — the token was in fact valid the whole time.
- Dynamic dropdowns that catch their own errors show generic "failed to load" placeholders, hiding the 401 entirely.
- The only fix is to **delete and recreate** the connection. Editing it in place does not help, because the stored `type` is what's wrong.

Diagnosing this took several hours and required reading the piece's git history. Nothing in the product pointed at the cause.

## Root cause

Three things compound:

**1. No type compatibility check at read time.** `getConnectionValue` in `packages/server/engine/src/lib/piece-context/connection-resolver.ts` passes `connection.value` straight through to the piece. There is no comparison against the auth methods the piece currently declares.

**2. No migration path.** There is no migration code anywhere under `packages/server/api/src/app/app-connection/`. `validateConnectionValue` in `app-connection-service.ts` switches on the *incoming* value's type at creation time and never cross-checks it against the piece's declared auth. Once stored, a value's type is never revisited.

**3. The status can never flip.** `needRefresh` (`app-connection.handler.ts:267`) only handles the OAuth2 variants and `CUSTOM_AUTH`. `SECRET_TEXT` falls through to the default and never refreshes, so it never reaches the `catch` block that would set `AppConnectionStatus.ERROR`. A static-token connection stays `ACTIVE` permanently regardless of whether it works. The only live check in the product is the manual **Revalidate** button, which exists solely on the Connections page — not in the flow builder, where users actually hit the problem.

Worth noting: connections already store `pieceVersion`, so the information needed to detect a stale value shape is present today.

## Scope

The bug is one piece today, but nothing prevents the next one.

28 pieces currently declare multi-method auth. 18 of them migrated from a single `PieceAuth.X()` to an array after connections could already exist. 17 of those 18 kept their original method and added others alongside it (`OAuth2 → [OAuth2, …]`, `CustomAuth → [CustomAuth, …]`), so existing connections still match a declared type and keep working.

SavvyCal is the only one that dropped its original type: `SecretText → [OAuth2, CustomAuth]`. That is the breaking shape, and it went unnoticed for three months because the platform reports the broken connection as `ACTIVE`.

`fathom` and `mistral-ai` made the same `SecretText`-to-array move but still declare `SecretText`, so they are unaffected — which is luck, not a guard rail. Nothing in review, CI, or runtime distinguishes their case from SavvyCal's.

## Suggested direction

Roughly in order of value:

1. **Detect and surface the mismatch.** When resolving a connection, compare `connection.value.type` against the piece's currently declared auth methods. On mismatch, set the connection to `ERROR` with an explicit message — "this connection was created with an authentication method this piece no longer supports, please reconnect" — instead of handing the piece a shape it can't read.
2. **Make the builder's status reflect reality**, rather than a stored value that some connection types can never update.
3. **Optionally, an auth migration hook** so piece authors can map an old stored shape onto a new one instead of forcing every user to reconnect.
4. **Optionally, a CI check** that flags when a piece version removes an auth type that a previous version declared — this is a breaking change for existing connections and currently passes review unnoticed.

Even just (1) would have turned this from a multi-hour investigation into a one-line message.

## Environment

- Activepieces Cloud (`cloud.activepieces.com`)
- Piece: `@activepieces/piece-savvycal` v0.1.6
- Connection created before 2026-05-06

issue.title: Piece selector tab labels truncated (e.g. "Approvals" shows as "Appr...")
issue.body: ## Bug description In the flow builder's piece selector, tab labels get cut off with an ellipsis even though there is plenty of horizontal space available (e.g. "Approvals" renders as "Appr...", "AI & Agents" as "AI & Ag..."). Since the truncated text has no tooltip, there's no way for a user to discover what the tab actually is. ## Screenshots ## Steps to reproduce 1. Open the flow builder and add/edit an action step to open the piece selector. 2. Look at the tab row (Explore, AI & Agents, Apps, Utility, Approvals). 3. Labels wider than ~85px are ellipsized mid-word. ## Root cause This is a regression introduced in `8ccf91b2ad` ("feat: customizable piece selector (#13824)"). Before that PR, `packages/web/src/features/pieces/components/piece-selector-tabs.tsx` rendered the label as: ```tsx {tab.name} ``` with the `TabsTrigger` using `grow` inside a CSS grid (`gridTemplateColumns: repeat(tabs.length, minmax(0, 1fr))`) — long labels simply wrapped to a second line. PR #13824 switched the tab row to a flex layout with a fixed-width trigger (`w-[85px] max-w-[85px]`) and added `truncate w-full text-center` to the label span, which turns any label wider than 85px into a single-line ellipsis cutoff instead of wrapping. ## Expected behavior Tab labels should be fully readable — either by sizing the tab to its content (there's visibly spare width in the row) or, if truncation is still needed at narrow viewport widths, by wrapping the label in `TextWithTooltip` so the full name is discoverable on hover, per this repo's own convention for overflowing text. ## Suggested fix Give each `TabsTrigger` an auto/min-width instead of a fixed max-width, and drop `truncate` in favor of `whitespace-nowrap` so labels render on one line at their natural width.

issue.title: [BUG]: flow-canvas nodes are announced as disabled buttons while being the control that opens the step
issue.body:
**Describe the bug** Every flow-canvas node that cannot be *dragged* is announced to assistive technology as a **disabled button**, even though clicking it is the only way to open the step. `packages/web/src/app/builder/flow-canvas/nodes/step-node/index.tsx:70-76` tells dnd-kit the node is not draggable for triggers and in the read-only builder: ```tsx const { attributes, listeners, setNodeRef } = useDraggable({ id: step.name, disabled: isTrigger || readonly, ... }); ``` `useDraggable`'s `attributes` in `@dnd-kit/core` 6.1.0 include `role: 'button'`, `tabIndex: 0`, `aria-roledescription: 'draggable'` and `aria-disabled: `. They are then spread onto the node container at line 149 — the same `
` that carries the click handler at line 147: ```tsx onClick={(e) => handleStepClick(e)} key={step.name} ref={isPieceSelectorOpened ? null : setNodeRef} {...stepNodeDivAttributes} {...stepNodeDivListeners} ``` So one element ends up saying `role="button"` and `aria-disabled="true"` at the same time, while being fully operable. The flag means "this cannot be dragged", but `aria-disabled` on a `role="button"` says "this button does nothing", and every consumer of the accessibility tree believes it: screen readers announce it as dimmed, and automation refuses to click it. Because the condition is `isTrigger || readonly`, this lands on: - the trigger node of every flow, including the `Select Trigger` placeholder on a brand-new flow, which is the first control a new user has to press; - **every** node in a run's read-only builder, which is step 4 of the procedure in `docs/flows/debugging-runs.mdx` — opening a step of a run to see what it did. **To Reproduce** 1. Sign in, create a new flow. The canvas shows the `1. Select Trigger` / `Empty Trigger` placeholder. 2. Read the placeholder off the DOM: ``` [role=button][aria-roledescription=draggable] count = 1
The page is fully hydrated in that screenshot — the breadcrumb, the 'You have unpublished changes' bar, the Publish button and the canvas toolbar are all rendered — so this is not a pre-hydration read. 4. Now bypass only the enabled-check, changing nothing else: ``` click({force: true}) returned after 3053 ms; [role=dialog] count = 1 dialog text: ExploreAppsUtility… ``` The trigger picker opens. The element receives the click, dispatches its handler and does its job. `aria-disabled="true"` is the only thing that was refusing it. The same attributes appear on every node when the builder is opened read-only for a run. **Expected behavior** The draggability flag should not be published as the button's enabled state. Two ways out, either of which fixes it: - keep dnd-kit's listeners and ref on the node but drop `aria-disabled` from what gets spread when the node is still clickable — e.g. spread `attributes` minus `aria-disabled`, since `role`/`tabIndex`/`aria-roledescription` are all still wanted; or - put the draggable attributes on a separate drag affordance and leave the clickable container as a plain button. A node a user can open should report itself as an enabled button. If a node in the read-only builder genuinely is inert, then `aria-disabled="true"` is right there and the click handler should be removed to match — but on the trigger placeholder of a new flow it is clearly wrong in the other direction. **Screenshots** Included above. **Additional context** Version 0.88.3, Community edition, Docker Compose with Postgres and Redis, at `d4cc3eaff77209b773f31e947b3b71306b02059d`. Chromium. Related in the same area: the project navigation strip renders `role="tab"` buttons whose `aria-selected` is `"false"` on all four tabs regardless of route (the active tab is marked only in `data-state="active"` and in styling), so a screen-reader user is not told which section they are in either. Happy to open that separately if it is useful.

issue.title: [BUG]: flow schema upgrade-on-read writes the whole trigger tree unconditionally, so a read can clobber a concurrent draft edit
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**

`flowVersionMigrationService.migrate` upgrades a stale `flow_version` row on read and writes the result back. The write is unconditional and it carries the entire `trigger` tree:

`packages/server/api/src/app/flows/flow-version/flow-version-migration.service.ts:44`

```ts
await flowVersionRepo().update(flowVersion.id, {
    schemaVersion: migratedFlowVersion.schemaVersion,
    ...spreadIfDefined('trigger', migratedFlowVersion.trigger),
    connectionIds: migratedFlowVersion.connectionIds,
    agentIds: migratedFlowVersion.agentIds,
    backupFiles,
})
```

It is reached from read paths, not from the edit path:

1. `flow-version.service.ts:334-339`, inside `findOne()`, which is the base read behind every version lookup
2. `flow.service.ts:220`, the flows-list populate path

So loading the flows page, or any request that resolves a flow version, can rewrite the trigger of a flow someone else is editing at that moment. Last writer wins and the other edit is gone with no conflict and no error, because the update matches on `id` alone and has no idea what it is overwriting.

**To Reproduce**

This is a race, so it is timing dependent rather than a click path. The shape of it:

1. Have a `flow_version` row whose `schemaVersion` is behind `LATEST_FLOW_SCHEMA_VERSION` (the normal state for every existing flow right after a release that bumps the schema).
2. Open that flow in the builder and start editing the draft.
3. While the edit is in flight, have anything else read the same flow, e.g. another user loading the flows list, or a second tab resolving the flow version.
4. The read-triggered migration write lands on top of the edit and the edited trigger tree is replaced by the migrated copy of the pre-edit trigger.

**Expected behavior**

An upgrade triggered by a read should not be able to overwrite a concurrent write. Either it takes the same per-flow lock the edit path takes, or it only writes when the row is still on the schema version it was read at.

**Why it is narrow**

`migrate` early-returns when the row already matches `LATEST_FLOW_SCHEMA_VERSION`, so it only writes for rows that are behind. In practice: after a release bumps the schema version every existing flow is stale until something reads it once, then it never writes again. The exposure is that window and it self-heals per flow. Still worth fixing though, because that window is exactly the moment after a deploy when everyone reloads the app at once.

**Suggested fix**

Make it a conditional write, so a losing upgrade no-ops instead of overwriting:

```ts
const schemaVersionAtRead = flowVersion.schemaVersion
const { affected } = await flowVersionRepo().update({
    id: flowVersion.id,
    schemaVersion: isNil(schemaVersionAtRead) ? IsNull() : schemaVersionAtRead,
}, {
    schemaVersion: migratedFlowVersion.schemaVersion,
    ...spreadIfDefined('trigger', migratedFlowVersion.trigger),
    connectionIds: migratedFlowVersion.connectionIds,
    agentIds: migratedFlowVersion.agentIds,
    backupFiles,
})
if (affected === 0) {
    // a concurrent writer already persisted this upgrade
}
```

`IsNull()` matters for legacy rows, because `schemaVersion` is nullable and a plain `undefined` in the where clause would drop the condition instead of matching NULL.

The catch: `affected === 0` now means "somebody else already persisted this upgrade", which is safe because the migration is idempotent and `migrate` still returns the migrated object to its caller, so nothing downstream changes shape. It does want a check that nothing relies on `migrate` having definitely written before it returns.

Alternatives we looked at: take a per-flow distributed lock around the write (heavier, and `migrate` is already called from inside a lock on some paths so it would have to be reentrant), or drop lazy upgrade-on-read entirely in favour of an explicit backfill after a schema bump and make reads read-only.

**Additional context**

Verified against `main` at 0.90.4. Happy to open a PR if that is useful, we are running the conditional-write version on our fork.

issue.title: [Pieces framework] Two auth methods of the same type silently resolve to the first one
issue.body:
## Summary

A piece can declare several authentication methods as an array (`auth: [a, b]`), and the UI renders a method picker for it. But the platform resolves *which* entry applies purely from the stored connection type:

```ts
// packages/pieces/framework/src/lib/property/authentication/index.ts
return pieceAuth.find(auth => authConnectionTypeToPropertyType[authValueType] === auth.type) ?? pieceAuth.at(0);
```

So two entries sharing a type — most commonly two `CustomAuth` — are indistinguishable, and **the first one always wins**. Nothing rejects this shape: the metadata schema is a plain array with no uniqueness constraint (`packages/pieces/framework/src/lib/piece-metadata.ts`), it type-checks, and the picker renders both methods correctly. The failure only appears when a user saves a connection.

## What breaks

- **Validation runs against the wrong method.** `validateAuth` in `packages/server/engine/src/lib/helper/piece-helper.ts` resolves through `getAuthPropertyForValue`, so the second method's credentials are checked by the first method's `validate()` — and rejected.
- **Reconnect preselects the wrong method** (`packages/web/src/app/connections/create-edit-connection-dialog.tsx`).
- **`refresh` support is read off `auth[0]`** unconditionally in `packages/server/api/src/app/app-connection/app-connection-service/app-connection.handler.ts`, so a `refresh` declared on a later entry is never detected.

## Why it is hard to avoid

Only `CUSTOM_AUTH` and `OIDC` accept arbitrary fields. `SecretText` and `BasicAuth` take no extra field, so **any method that needs its own URL must be a `CustomAuth`** — which makes this bite precisely the self-hosted pieces, where each method needs an instance URL alongside the credentials.

Umami avoids it only by coincidence: its split is cloud (fixed URL → `SecretText`) vs self-hosted (`CustomAuth`), so the URL falls on one side. A piece whose methods split by *credential kind* rather than by *hosting* has no such escape.

`OIDC` technically accepts free-form props, but it means OpenID Connect identity federation (used by the AWS pieces for assume-role, with a server-signed key) — using it as a second `CustomAuth` slot would misrepresent the connection type in the database.

## The workaround, and what it costs

The current fallback is a single `CustomAuth` holding every field from both methods, plus a `StaticDropdown` to name the intent and MarkDown blocks telling users to leave the other section blank — see `packages/pieces/community/baserow/src/lib/auth.ts`.

It cannot be improved, because `CustomAuthProps` only accepts static properties (no `DynamicProperties`, no `refreshers`), so there is no way to show or hide fields based on the dropdown. Every user sees every field of both methods on one page, and the dropdown is read only at runtime — the UI ignores it.

## This has already cost the project

- #12226 (merged 8 Apr) shipped Baserow with `baserowAuth = [databaseTokenAuth, jwtAuth]` — two `CustomAuth`.
- #12504 was opened 9 Apr, the day after, following that pattern for Postiz.
- #12759 (23 Apr) removed JWT auth from Baserow entirely; the array form did not work.
- #12964 (29 Apr) restored it as the single-`CustomAuth`-plus-dropdown workaround above.
- #12504 was closed 2 Jun: *"Multiple auths of the same type (`CustomAuth`) are not supported in a piece."* Correct — but the pattern it used was in `main` when it was written, and the replacement pattern had landed five weeks earlier.

Since nothing enforces the constraint, the next piece author will reach for the array form the same way.

## Proposed direction

Give auth properties an explicit discriminator (e.g. an `id`), persist it on the connection, and resolve through it in `getAuthPropertyForValue`, falling back to the current type matching when absent. That is the smallest change that makes the existing multi-auth mechanism actually general, rather than adding a second mechanism alongside it.

Two things to settle before implementing:

- **Migration of existing connections.** #14992 already reports that changing a piece's declared auth silently breaks connections created under the old shape — the same machinery, so the two should be designed together.
- **Whether to instead reject duplicate types at metadata validation**, as a cheap first step, so the failure is loud at build time instead of silent at connection time.

Happy to implement this — raising it first so the direction can be agreed before any code, given it touches the framework, the engine, the server and the web app.

It cannot be improved, because `CustomAuthProps` only accepts static properties (no `DynamicProperties`, no `refreshers`), so there is no way to show or hide fields based on the dropdown. Every user sees every field of both methods on one page, and the dropdown is read only at runtime — the UI ignores it.

## This has already cost the project

- #12226 (merged 8 Apr) shipped Baserow with `baserowAuth = [databaseTokenAuth, jwtAuth]` — two `CustomAuth`.
- #12504 was opened 9 Apr, the day after, following that pattern for Postiz.
- #12759 (23 Apr) removed JWT auth from Baserow entirely; the array form did not work.
- #12964 (29 Apr) restored it as the single-`CustomAuth`-plus-dropdown workaround above.
- #12504 was closed 2 Jun: *"Multiple auths of the same type (`CustomAuth`) are not supported in a piece."* Correct — but the pattern it used was in `main` when it was written, and the replacement pattern had landed five weeks earlier.

Since nothing enforces the constraint, the next piece author will reach for the array form the same way.

## Proposed direction

Give auth properties an explicit discriminator (e.g. an `id`), persist it on the connection, and resolve through it in `getAuthPropertyForValue`, falling back to the current type matching when absent. That is the smallest change that makes the existing multi-auth mechanism actually general, rather than adding a second mechanism alongside it.

Two things to settle before implementing:

- **Migration of existing connections.** #14992 already reports that changing a piece's declared auth silently breaks connections created under the old shape — the same machinery, so the two should be designed together.
- **Whether to instead reject duplicate types at metadata validation**, as a cheap first step, so the failure is loud at build time instead of silent at connection time.

Happy to implement this — raising it first so the direction can be agreed before any code, given it touches the framework, the engine, the server and the web app.

issue.title: [BUG]: flow schema upgrade-on-read writes the whole trigger tree unconditionally, so a read can clobber a concurrent draft edit
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**

`flowVersionMigrationService.migrate` upgrades a stale `flow_version` row on read and writes the result back. The write is unconditional and it carries the entire `trigger` tree:

`packages/server/api/src/app/flows/flow-version/flow-version-migration.service.ts:44`

```ts
await flowVersionRepo().update(flowVersion.id, {
    schemaVersion: migratedFlowVersion.schemaVersion,
    ...spreadIfDefined('trigger', migratedFlowVersion.trigger),
    connectionIds: migratedFlowVersion.connectionIds,
    agentIds: migratedFlowVersion.agentIds,
    backupFiles,
})
```

It is reached from read paths, not from the edit path:

1. `flow-version.service.ts:334-339`, inside `findOne()`, which is the base read behind every version lookup
2. `flow.service.ts:220`, the flows-list populate path

So loading the flows page, or any request that resolves a flow version, can rewrite the trigger of a flow someone else is editing at that moment. Last writer wins and the other edit is gone with no conflict and no error, because the update matches on `id` alone and has no idea what it is overwriting.

**To Reproduce**

This is a race, so it is timing dependent rather than a click path. The shape of it:

1. Have a `flow_version` row whose `schemaVersion` is behind `LATEST_FLOW_SCHEMA_VERSION` (the normal state for every existing flow right after a release that bumps the schema).
2. Open that flow in the builder and start editing the draft.
3. While the edit is in flight, have anything else read the same flow, e.g. another user loading the flows list, or a second tab resolving the flow version.
4. The read-triggered migration write lands on top of the edit and the edited trigger tree is replaced by the migrated copy of the pre-edit trigger.

**Expected behavior**

An upgrade triggered by a read should not be able to overwrite a concurrent write. Either it takes the same per-flow lock the edit path takes, or it only writes when the row is still on the schema version it was read at.

**Why it is narrow**

`migrate` early-returns when the row already matches `LATEST_FLOW_SCHEMA_VERSION`, so it only writes for rows that are behind. In practice: after a release bumps the schema version every existing flow is stale until something reads it once, then it never writes again. The exposure is that window and it self-heals per flow. Still worth fixing though, because that window is exactly the moment after a deploy when everyone reloads the app at once.

**Suggested fix**

Make it a conditional write, so a losing upgrade no-ops instead of overwriting:

```ts
const schemaVersionAtRead = flowVersion.schemaVersion
const { affected } = await flowVersionRepo().update({
    id: flowVersion.id,
    schemaVersion: isNil(schemaVersionAtRead) ? IsNull() : schemaVersionAtRead,
}, {
    schemaVersion: migratedFlowVersion.schemaVersion,
    ...spreadIfDefined('trigger', migratedFlowVersion.trigger),
    connectionIds: migratedFlowVersion.connectionIds,
    agentIds: migratedFlowVersion.agentIds,
    backupFiles,
})
if (affected === 0) {
    // a concurrent writer already persisted this upgrade
}
```

`IsNull()` matters for legacy rows, because `schemaVersion` is nullable and a plain `undefined` in the where clause would drop the condition instead of matching NULL.

The catch: `affected === 0` now means "somebody else already persisted this upgrade", which is safe because the migration is idempotent and `migrate` still returns the migrated object to its caller, so nothing downstream changes shape. It does want a check that nothing relies on `migrate` having definitely written before it returns.

Alternatives we looked at: take a per-flow distributed lock around the write (heavier, and `migrate` is already called from inside a lock on some paths so it would have to be reentrant), or drop lazy upgrade-on-read entirely in favour of an explicit backfill after a schema bump and make reads read-only.

**Additional context**

Verified against `main` at 0.90.4. Happy to open a PR if that is useful, we are running the conditional-write version on our fork.

issue.title: [BUG]: formula arguments keep the space after each semicolon, so the reference page's own examples return wrong values
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**

Formula arguments keep the space that the reference page's own examples put after each `;` separator. The space becomes part of the argument value, so every worked example on the formulas page produces a different result from the one the page prints.

`splitArgsBySemicolon` (`packages/.../formula-evaluator.ts:358-388`) splits on semicolons at paren depth 0 and never trims the pieces. So in `if(1500 > 1000; High value; Standard)` the second argument is literally `" High value"`, with the leading space.

Copying four examples from the reference page character for character:

| formula, exactly as the docs print it | returned | the docs print |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `if(1500 > 1000; High value; Standard)` | `" High value"` | `High value` |
| `combine(John; Smith; " ")` | `"John  Smith"` | `John Smith` |
| `filter_list(<3 tickets>; status; open)` | `[]` | the two open tickets |
| `format_date(2025-01-15; MMM DD, YYYY)` | `" Jan 01, 2009"` | `Jan 01, 2009` |

Removing the spaces makes each one produce the printed result, so the space is the whole difference.

The `filter_list` row is why this is not cosmetic. The property name arrives as `" status"`, matches no key on any ticket, and the predicate returns an **empty list with no error**. Someone following the page exactly gets a silently wrong answer, and nothing anywhere reports a problem. In an automation that means a branch that should act on two open tickets acts on none.

Quoting fixes it, `format_date("2025-01-15"; "MMM DD, YYYY")` returns `Jan 15, 2025`. But the reference page never says quotes are required except for empty and single-space values, and it prints all 109 of its examples with a space after each separator.

Either the splitter should trim its arguments, or the page's examples should be rewritten without the spaces. As it stands the documentation and the evaluator disagree on every example.

Note the last row also carries a second, separate defect, the `2009` is `2025 - 1 - 15` evaluated as arithmetic, which is already reported as #14761. This report is only about the space.

**To Reproduce**

1. Create a flow with any trigger and a step whose input is a formula.
2. Set the formula to `if(1500 > 1000; High value; Standard)`, exactly as the reference page prints it.
3. Test the step and read the returned value.

Returns `" High value"` with a leading space. Same procedure reproduces each row of the table above.

**Expected behavior**

A formula copied from the reference page returns the value that page prints, and `filter_list` either matches the property or reports that it cannot, rather than silently returning an empty list.

**Additional context**

Reproduced on a Community instance built from source at `d4cc3eaff77209b773f31e947b3b71306b02059d` (0.88.3), Postgres and Redis via the repo's own compose, on macOS. Reproduced twice in independent runs, and separately by hand one `POST /api/v1/sample-data/test-step` per pair.

One root cause sits under four separate failures in our test corpus, which is why it is worth fixing rather than documenting.

Suggested labels: `bug`

issue.title: [BUG]: the formula reference prints percentage(75; 100) as 75%, the function returns 75
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**

The Number table in `docs/flows/formula-reference.mdx` prints `percentage`'s example output with a percent sign:

> \| `percentage` \| `percentage(value; total)` \| Calculates what percentage the value is of the total. \| `percentage(75; 100)` → `75%` \|

(line 68). The evaluator returns the bare number `75`. The same string is also `exampleResult: '75%'` in `packages/core/formula/src/lib/function-registry.ts:428`, which is what the builder's hover popover shows, so the user is told `75%` in two places and gets `75`.

`packages/core/formula/src/lib/function-implementations.ts:138-142`:

```ts
parser.functions.percentage = (n: unknown, total: unknown) => {
    const divisor = Number(total)
    if (divisor === 0) throw new Error('Division by zero')
    return (Number(n) / divisor) * 100
}
```

and the registry entry declares `returnType: 'number'` alongside the `'75%'` example, so the row and the type it sits next to already disagree.

**To Reproduce**

1. Sign in and create a flow.
2. `POST /api/v1/flows/{flowId}` with `type: "IMPORT_FLOW"`, a Catch Webhook trigger and a Return Response step whose body is:

```json
{"fields": {"status": 200, "headers": {}, "body": {"value": "ap-formula-v1::{percentage(75; 100)}::ap-formula-v1"}}, "respond": "stop", "responseType": "json"}
```

3. `POST /api/v1/webhooks/{flowId}/draft/sync` with any JSON body. The `/sync` form waits for the flow to finish, so the response is the settled value:

```
200
{"value":75}
```

The doc row prints `75%`.

We tried it with and without the space after the semicolon — `percentage(75; 100)` and `percentage(75;100)` — and got `75` both times, so this is not the argument-whitespace issue in #15051; numeric arguments are parsed as numbers either way.

**Expected behavior**

Either the row prints what the function returns:

```
| `percentage` | `percentage(value; total)` | Calculates what percentage the value is of the total. | `percentage(75; 100)` → `75` |
```

or `percentage` formats its result the way its neighbours in the same table already do. The two rows just below it are the control — those functions *do* attach their symbol, and their rows are accurate:

```ts
parser.functions.format_currency = (n, symbol = '$') => `${String(symbol)}${Number(n).toFixed(2)}`
parser.functions.cents_to_dollars = (n) => `$${(Number(n) / 100).toFixed(2)}`
```

`format_currency(49.99; "$")` → `$49.99` and `cents_to_dollars(4999)` → `$49.99`, exactly as printed. `percentage` is the only row in the Number table whose printed output carries a unit the function does not produce.

Correcting the doc row looks like the right call, since `returnType: 'number'` says a number is the intent and a caller doing arithmetic on the result would break if the `%` were added. If so, `exampleResult` in `function-registry.ts:428` needs the same fix, or the hover popover will keep showing `75%`.

**Screenshots**

N/A — reproduced over the API.

**Additional context**

Version 0.88.3, Community edition, Docker Compose with Postgres and Redis, at `d4cc3eaff77209b773f31e947b3b71306b02059d`.
