issue.title: [BUG]: formulas with the wrong argument count, or with commas instead of semicolons, run anyway instead of failing the step
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**

`docs/flows/using-formulas.mdx` states two rules about formula arguments:

> Arguments are separated by **semicolons (`;`)**, not commas.

(line 32), and, after listing "**Wrong number of values** — you have too few or too many arguments":

> The flow won't run a step whose function is in error — fix it before publishing.

(line 141).

Neither rule holds when the flow actually runs. A formula with too many arguments, with too few, or with commas in place of semicolons runs to `SUCCEEDED` and silently produces a value.

`packages/core/formula/src/lib/function-registry.ts` does declare `minArgs`/`maxArgs` for every function, but the only code that reads them to raise an error is `typeCheckTiptapDoc` (`packages/core/formula/src/lib/function-type-checker.ts:41-57`), and its only two call sites in the whole tree are browser-side:

```
packages/web/src/app/builder/piece-properties/text-input-with-mentions/tiptap-editor.tsx:670
packages/web/src/app/builder/piece-properties/text-input-with-mentions/tiptap-editor.tsx:781
```

The evaluator and the worker never check. So the check exists only for a person typing into the builder, while the sentence that documents it is a statement about *running*. A flow that arrives any other way — `IMPORT_FLOW`, a template, an API client, a copy/paste of a step — is never checked and runs whatever it was given.

The failure mode is the one a user is least able to notice: the formula they wrote is not the formula that ran, and nothing anywhere says so.

**To Reproduce**

*Too many arguments.* `uppercase` declares `minArgs: 1, maxArgs: 1`.

1. Sign in and create a flow.
2. `POST /api/v1/flows/{flowId}` with `type: "IMPORT_FLOW"`, a Catch Webhook trigger and one Advanced Mapping step whose mapping is:

```json
{"mapping": {"value": "ap-formula-v1::{uppercase(a; b)}::ap-formula-v1"}}
```

3. `POST /api/v1/sample-data/test-step` → `{"projectId": "...", "flowVersionId": "...", "stepName": "step_1"}` → `200`
4. `GET /api/v1/flow-runs/{runId}` once the run has finished:

```json
{"id":"2qC93vIxjXHgtgVyHJFJS","status":"SUCCEEDED","finishTime":"2026-08-21T02:38:59.663Z","stepsCount":1,
 "steps":{"trigger":{"type":"PIECE_TRIGGER","status":"SUCCEEDED","input":{},"output":{}},
          "step_1":{"type":"PIECE","status":"SUCCEEDED","input":{"mapping":{"value":"A"}},
                    "output":{"value":"A"},"duration":101.89495800000077}}}
```

The run reached a terminal state with `finishTime` set. The second argument was discarded in silence.

*Commas instead of semicolons.* Same flow shape, mapping value:

```json
{"mapping": {"value": "ap-formula-v1::{combine(\"John\",\"Smith\",\" \")}::ap-formula-v1"}}
```

```json
{"id":"obodzLfSccnRX7J0j093C","status":"SUCCEEDED","finishTime":"2026-08-21T02:39:06.511Z","stepsCount":1,
 "steps":{"trigger":{"type":"PIECE_TRIGGER","status":"SUCCEEDED","input":{},"output":{}},
          "step_1":{"type":"PIECE","status":"SUCCEEDED","input":{"mapping":{"value":"John Smith"}},
                    "output":{"value":"John Smith"},"duration":80.05720800000199}}}
```

The comma form the guide names as an error is not merely accepted — it produces the *same* answer as the documented semicolon form, which is what guarantees nobody ever finds out the rule was broken. The control, `combine("John";"Smith";" ")` through `POST /api/v1/webhooks/{flowId}/draft/sync`, answers `{"value":"John Smith"}` as well.

Other forms we tried, one flow each, same route:

| formula | declared arity | evaluates to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `uppercase(a; b)` | 1..1 | `"A"` |
| `uppercase(a;b)` | 1..1 | `"A"` |
| `uppercase(a, b)` | 1..1 | `"A, B"` |
| `combine("John")` | 2..3 | `"John"` |
| `combine("John","Smith"," ")` | 2..3 | `"John Smith"` |
| `combine(John,Smith," ")` | 2..3 | `"John,Smith,\" \""` |
| `if(1>0;yes)` | 3..3 | `"yes"` |
| `if(1>0;a;b;c;d)` | 3..3 | `"a"` |

Neither bound is enforced in either direction, for either function. `combine` has no `argCompatibility.defaultArgs` entry, so `combine("John")` is not the back-compat padding in `function-implementations.ts:414-423` — it is simply unchecked.

**Expected behavior**

One of the two has to give. Either:

- a step whose formula has the wrong argument count, or comma separators, fails the run with the error the editor already knows how to phrase (`function-type-checker.ts` produces "accepts at most N values, but got M"), which is what `using-formulas.mdx:141` promises; or
- the arity and separator rules are enforced at the evaluator, so a formula that is going to be silently rewritten is rejected where it is saved rather than where it is typed; or
- the docs stop promising a run-time gate that only the editor performs, and say plainly that commas are accepted.

The middle option seems closest to the intent, since the registry already carries the bounds and the message text already exists.

**Screenshots**

N/A — reproduced entirely over the API.

**Additional context**

Version 0.88.3, Community edition, Docker Compose with Postgres and Redis, at `d4cc3eaff77209b773f31e947b3b71306b02059d`.

This is separate from the editor-side arity work in #14573 / #14590, which was about the builder's check *over*-firing. This report is the opposite: the check never fires anywhere outside the builder.

issue.title: [BUG]: the formula reference prints percentage(75; 100) as 75%, the function returns 75
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**

The Number table in `docs/flows/formula-reference.mdx` prints `percentage`'s example output with a percent sign:

> \| `percentage` \| `percentage(value; total)` \| Calculates what percentage the value is of the total. \| `percentage(75; 100)` → `75%` \|

(line 68). The evaluator returns the bare number `75`. The same string is also `exampleResult: '75%'` in `packages/core/formula/src/lib/function-registry.ts:428`, which is what the builder's hover popover shows, so the user is told `75%` in two places and gets `75`.

`packages/core/formula/src/lib/function-implementations.ts:138-142`:

```ts
parser.functions.percentage = (n: unknown, total: unknown) => {
    const divisor = Number(total)
    if (divisor === 0) throw new Error('Division by zero')
    return (Number(n) / divisor) * 100
}
```

and the registry entry declares `returnType: 'number'` alongside the `'75%'` example, so the row and the type it sits next to already disagree.

**To Reproduce**

1. Sign in and create a flow.
2. `POST /api/v1/flows/{flowId}` with `type: "IMPORT_FLOW"`, a Catch Webhook trigger and a Return Response step whose body is:

```json
{"fields": {"status": 200, "headers": {}, "body": {"value": "ap-formula-v1::{percentage(75; 100)}::ap-formula-v1"}}, "respond": "stop", "responseType": "json"}
```

3. `POST /api/v1/webhooks/{flowId}/draft/sync` with any JSON body. The `/sync` form waits for the flow to finish, so the response is the settled value:

```
200
{"value":75}
```

The doc row prints `75%`.

We tried it with and without the space after the semicolon — `percentage(75; 100)` and `percentage(75;100)` — and got `75` both times, so this is not the argument-whitespace issue in #15051; numeric arguments are parsed as numbers either way.

**Expected behavior**

Either the row prints what the function returns:

```
| `percentage` | `percentage(value; total)` | Calculates what percentage the value is of the total. | `percentage(75; 100)` → `75` |
```

or `percentage` formats its result the way its neighbours in the same table already do. The two rows just below it are the control — those functions *do* attach their symbol, and their rows are accurate:

```ts
parser.functions.format_currency = (n, symbol = '$') => `${String(symbol)}${Number(n).toFixed(2)}`
parser.functions.cents_to_dollars = (n) => `$${(Number(n) / 100).toFixed(2)}`
```

`format_currency(49.99; "$")` → `$49.99` and `cents_to_dollars(4999)` → `$49.99`, exactly as printed. `percentage` is the only row in the Number table whose printed output carries a unit the function does not produce.

Correcting the doc row looks like the right call, since `returnType: 'number'` says a number is the intent and a caller doing arithmetic on the result would break if the `%` were added. If so, `exampleResult` in `function-registry.ts:428` needs the same fix, or the hover popover will keep showing `75%`.

**Screenshots**

N/A — reproduced over the API.

**Additional context**

Version 0.88.3, Community edition, Docker Compose with Postgres and Redis, at `d4cc3eaff77209b773f31e947b3b71306b02059d`.

issue.title: [BUG]: flow-canvas nodes are announced as disabled buttons while being the control that opens the step
issue.body:
**Describe the bug** Every flow-canvas node that cannot be *dragged* is announced to assistive technology as a **disabled button**, even though clicking it is the only way to open the step. `packages/web/src/app/builder/flow-canvas/nodes/step-node/index.tsx:70-76` tells dnd-kit the node is not draggable for triggers and in the read-only builder: ```tsx const { attributes, listeners, setNodeRef } = useDraggable({ id: step.name, disabled: isTrigger || readonly, ... }); ``` `useDraggable`'s `attributes` in `@dnd-kit/core` 6.1.0 include `role: 'button'`, `tabIndex: 0`, `aria-roledescription: 'draggable'` and `aria-disabled: `. They are then spread onto the node container at line 149 — the same `
` that carries the click handler at line 147: ```tsx onClick={(e) => handleStepClick(e)} key={step.name} ref={isPieceSelectorOpened ? null : setNodeRef} {...stepNodeDivAttributes} {...stepNodeDivListeners} ``` So one element ends up saying `role="button"` and `aria-disabled="true"` at the same time, while being fully operable. The flag means "this cannot be dragged", but `aria-disabled` on a `role="button"` says "this button does nothing", and every consumer of the accessibility tree believes it: screen readers announce it as dimmed, and automation refuses to click it. Because the condition is `isTrigger || readonly`, this lands on: - the trigger node of every flow, including the `Select Trigger` placeholder on a brand-new flow, which is the first control a new user has to press; - **every** node in a run's read-only builder, which is step 4 of the procedure in `docs/flows/debugging-runs.mdx` — opening a step of a run to see what it did. **To Reproduce** 1. Sign in, create a new flow. The canvas shows the `1. Select Trigger` / `Empty Trigger` placeholder. 2. Read the placeholder off the DOM: ``` [role=button][aria-roledescription=draggable] count = 1
The page is fully hydrated in that screenshot — the breadcrumb, the 'You have unpublished changes' bar, the Publish button and the canvas toolbar are all rendered — so this is not a pre-hydration read. 4. Now bypass only the enabled-check, changing nothing else: ``` click({force: true}) returned after 3053 ms; [role=dialog] count = 1 dialog text: ExploreAppsUtility… ``` The trigger picker opens. The element receives the click, dispatches its handler and does its job. `aria-disabled="true"` is the only thing that was refusing it. The same attributes appear on every node when the builder is opened read-only for a run. **Expected behavior** The draggability flag should not be published as the button's enabled state. Two ways out, either of which fixes it: - keep dnd-kit's listeners and ref on the node but drop `aria-disabled` from what gets spread when the node is still clickable — e.g. spread `attributes` minus `aria-disabled`, since `role`/`tabIndex`/`aria-roledescription` are all still wanted; or - put the draggable attributes on a separate drag affordance and leave the clickable container as a plain button. A node a user can open should report itself as an enabled button. issue.title: [BUG]: flow schema upgrade-on-read writes the whole trigger tree unconditionally, so a read can clobber a concurrent draft edit
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**

`flowVersionMigrationService.migrate` upgrades a stale `flow_version` row on read and writes the result back. The write is unconditional and it carries the entire `trigger` tree:

`packages/server/api/src/app/flows/flow-version/flow-version-migration.service.ts:44`

```ts
await flowVersionRepo().update(flowVersion.id, {
    schemaVersion: migratedFlowVersion.schemaVersion,
    ...spreadIfDefined('trigger', migratedFlowVersion.trigger),
    connectionIds: migratedFlowVersion.connectionIds,
    agentIds: migratedFlowVersion.agentIds,
    backupFiles,
})
```

It is reached from read paths, not from the edit path:

1. `flow-version.service.ts:334-339`, inside `findOne()`, which is the base read behind every version lookup
2. `flow.service.ts:220`, the flows-list populate path

So loading the flows page, or any request that resolves a flow version, can rewrite the trigger of a flow someone else is editing at that moment. Last writer wins and the other edit is gone with no conflict and no error, because the update matches on `id` alone and has no idea what it is overwriting.

**To Reproduce**

This is a race, so it is timing dependent rather than a click path. The shape of it:

1. Have a `flow_version` row whose `schemaVersion` is behind `LATEST_FLOW_SCHEMA_VERSION` (the normal state for every existing flow right after a release that bumps the schema).
2. Open that flow in the builder and start editing the draft.
3. While the edit is in flight, have anything else read the same flow, e.g. another user loading the flows list, or a second tab resolving the flow version.
4. The read-triggered migration write lands on top of the edit and the edited trigger tree is replaced by the migrated copy of the pre-edit trigger.

**Expected behavior**

An upgrade triggered by a read should not be able to overwrite a concurrent write. Either it takes the same per-flow lock the edit path takes, or it only writes when the row is still on the schema version it was read at.

**Why it is narrow**

`migrate` early-returns when the row already matches `LATEST_FLOW_SCHEMA_VERSION`, so it only writes for rows that are behind. In practice: after a release bumps the schema version every existing flow is stale until something reads it once, then it never writes again. The exposure is that window and it self-heals per flow. Still worth fixing though, because that window is exactly the moment after a deploy when everyone reloads the app at once.

**Suggested fix**

Make it a conditional write, so a losing upgrade no-ops instead of overwriting:

```ts
const schemaVersionAtRead = flowVersion.schemaVersion
const { affected } = await flowVersionRepo().update({
    id: flowVersion.id,
    schemaVersion: isNil(schemaVersionAtRead) ? IsNull() : schemaVersionAtRead,
}, {
    schemaVersion: migratedFlowVersion.schemaVersion,
    ...spreadIfDefined('trigger', migratedFlowVersion.trigger),
    connectionIds: migratedFlowVersion.connectionIds,
    agentIds: migratedFlowVersion.agentIds,
    backupFiles,
})
if (affected === 0) {
    // a concurrent writer already persisted this upgrade
}
```

`IsNull()` matters for legacy rows, because `schemaVersion` is nullable and a plain `undefined` in the where clause would drop the condition instead of matching NULL.

The catch: `affected === 0` now means "somebody else already persisted this upgrade", which is safe because the migration is idempotent and `migrate` still returns the migrated object to its caller, so nothing downstream changes shape. It does want a check that nothing relies on `migrate` having definitely written before it returns.

Alternatives we looked at: take a per-flow distributed lock around the write (heavier, and `migrate` is already called from inside a lock on some paths so it would have to be reentrant), or drop lazy upgrade-on-read entirely in favour of an explicit backfill after a schema bump and make reads read-only.

**Additional context**

Verified against `main` at 0.90.4. Happy to open a PR if that is useful, we are running the conditional-write version on our fork.

issue.title: Docs: the Railway install guide deploy button returns 404 (fix branch ready)

issue.title: [i18n] French translations in production: what is still broken, and a fix for each (supersedes #13530)
issue.body:
I opened #13530 in June. I've re-checked every point against the current state (latest `l10n_main` export and Crowdin project settings, 2026-09-17). Two claims there were inaccurate, several problems got worse, and there are new ones. This issue replaces it with verified facts and one concrete fix per problem.

## Summary

| # | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | No translation has reached `main` since 2026-06-20 | Rotate `CROWDIN_PRS`, alert on stale l10n PRs |
| 2 | Broken machine translations still ship in 100+ pieces | Roll back + CI check on technical identifiers |
| 3 | The Custom API Call block is translated separately in every piece | Exclude it from translation extraction |
| 4 | The piece docs teach the workflow that Crowdin overwrites | Update the docs page, CONTRIBUTING and PR template |
| 5 | Unreviewed and untranslated strings ship as-is | Document proofreader access, review export settings |

## 1. No translation has reached `main` since 2026-06-20

The last merged Crowdin PR is #13815 (2026-06-20). #13894 then stayed open until 2026-09-08, because the required `Lint PR` check rejects the title "New Crowdin updates". Its replacement #15370 is still open: the `Auto Merge Crowdin PRs Action` run of 2026-09-10 failed with `HttpError: Bad credentials`.

Nothing alerted anyone for almost three months.
→ Rotate `CROWDIN_PRS`, and fail a scheduled job when the newest l10n PR is older than N days.

## 2. Broken machine translations still ship

From the latest `l10n_main` export (757 `fr.json`):

| Source | Shipped French | Pieces |
|---|---|---|
| `PUT` | "EFFACER" (= erase) | 133 |
| `GET` / `POST` / `DELETE` | "OBTENIR" / "POSTER" / "SUPPRIMER" | 133 |
| `HEAD` | "TÊTE" | 121 |
| `First Name` | "First Name" (left untranslated) | 96 |
| `Text` | "Texte du texte" ("text of the text") | 53 |
| `Page Size` | "Nombre d'élément" | 29 |
| `Table` | "Tableau" (grid view, not a database table) | 14 |
| `Upsert Row` | "Lignée supérieure" ("upper lineage") | 3 |

The HTTP methods are the worst: picking "EFFACER" in the method dropdown sends a PUT.
→ Add a CI check that technical identifiers (HTTP methods, `JSON`, placeholders) stay verbatim, and roll back the existing damage.

## 3. The Custom API Call block is translated separately in every piece

`createCustomApiCallAction` (`packages/pieces/common`) is extracted into each piece's `translation.json`, so Crowdin holds 479 separate French copies of the same form, each pre-translated independently. They disagree: `Headers` is "En-têtes" in 209 pieces and "Headers" in 267.

This is a technical form for raw HTTP calls, and its vocabulary is English. #15248 (2026-09-07) redesigned it (`Timeout`, `Return Error as Output`, `URL`, `JSON Body`…). Pieces depend on `pieces-common` via `workspace:*`, so every regeneration of a piece's `translation.json` pushes the new labels as new strings — ~479 pieces × 8 languages, all pre-translated again.
→ Exclude the block from extraction (`generateTranslationFileFromPiece` / `pieceTranslation.pathsToValuesToTranslate`) or mark it do-not-translate, and reset the existing translations.

## 4. The piece docs teach the workflow that Crowdin overwrites

`docs/build-pieces/piece-reference/i18n.mdx` tells piece authors to copy `translation.json` to `fr.json` and translate it themselves; Crowdin appears only as a tip. Crowdin's sync later replaces that file, so the work is silently lost. `CONTRIBUTING.md` and the PR template don't mention translations at all.
(Correction to #13530: `docs/about/i18n.mdx` does describe Crowdin, since 2023.)
→ Make Crowdin the only documented path on that page, and add one line to `CONTRIBUTING.md` and the PR template.

## 5. Unreviewed and untranslated strings ship as-is

Current project settings: AI pre-translation is on for all 8 languages, TM pre-translation auto-approves 100% matches, and `exportApprovedOnly` and `skipUntranslatedStrings` are both `false`. Untranslated strings therefore ship as English copies — the Outseta `fr.json` on `main` contains `"Account Created": "Account Created"` — and unreviewed AI output ships as if reviewed.

Approval is the only lock. (Correction to #13530: translators *can* approve — I was granted proofreader rights — but nothing documents how to ask for them.)
→ Document how to request proofreader access for a locale, and confirm pre-translation never replaces an existing human translation.

## Related

- #15586 — auth texts of pieces with several auth methods are never translated (30 pieces)

I maintain 14 pieces and keep their French approved in Crowdin. Happy to help test any of these changes.

issue.title: [BUG] A worker can stay connected without polling when its settings acknowledgment is missed
issue.body:
## Describe the bug

A worker can look connected to the API and still never begin consuming jobs. This happens when its first request for settings does not receive an acknowledgment. There is no timeout on that request and no second attempt while the socket remains open.

The worker's `connect` handler awaits `fetchAndStoreSettings` before calling `startPollingWorkers`. The API's `FETCH_WORKER_SETTINGS` handler first awaits `machineService.onConnection` and only then calls the acknowledgment callback. When that operation rejects, the websocket wrapper logs the rejected promise but neither replies to the waiting worker nor disconnects it. The worker is left awaiting a callback that will not arrive.

The poll-loop watchdog cannot recover this state because no poll loop has been registered yet. In a combined app-and-worker process, the API can remain available while that worker is idle.

## To reproduce

1. Start an API and a worker, with at least one job waiting in the queue.
2. On the first `FETCH_WORKER_SETTINGS` request, make `machineService.onConnection` reject once before the server calls its acknowledgment callback. Keep the Socket.IO connection open.
3. Observe that the worker has connected but makes no poll requests and does not pick up the waiting job.
4. Reconnect the socket. The worker requests settings again and begins polling once that request succeeds.

## Expected behavior

The worker should bound the wait for settings and retry or reconnect after a missed acknowledgment. It should begin polling only after receiving and storing valid settings. A transient setup failure should not require an operator to restart an otherwise connected worker.

## Additional context

- Worker startup and unbounded acknowledgment wait: `packages/server/worker/src/lib/worker.ts`, in the socket `connect` handler and `fetchAndStoreSettings`.
- Server callback ordering: `packages/server/api/src/app/workers/machine/machine-controller.ts`, in the `FETCH_WORKER_SETTINGS` listener.
- Rejection handling: `packages/server/api/src/app/core/websockets.service.ts` and `packages/server/api/src/app/helper/promise-handler.ts`.
- A separate setup path in `fetchAndStoreSettings` returns after a machine-info error without storing settings; that path should also avoid starting job polling.

issue.title: [Pieces framework] Two auth methods of the same type silently resolve to the first one
issue.body:
## Summary

A piece can declare several authentication methods as an array (`auth: [a, b]`), and the UI renders a method picker for it. But the platform resolves *which* entry applies purely from the stored connection type:

```ts
// packages/pieces/framework/src/lib/property/authentication/index.ts
return pieceAuth.find(auth => authConnectionTypeToPropertyType[authValueType] === auth.type) ?? pieceAuth.at(0);
```

So two entries sharing a type — most commonly two `CustomAuth` — are indistinguishable, and **the first one always wins**. Nothing rejects this shape: the metadata schema is a plain array with no uniqueness constraint (`packages/pieces/framework/src/lib/piece-metadata.ts`), it type-checks, and the picker renders both methods correctly. The failure only appears when a user saves a connection.

## What breaks

- **Validation runs against the wrong method.** `validateAuth` in `packages/server/engine/src/lib/helper/piece-helper.ts` resolves through `getAuthPropertyForValue`, so the second method's credentials are checked by the first method's `validate()` — and rejected.
- **Reconnect preselects the wrong method** (`packages/web/src/app/connections/create-edit-connection-dialog.tsx`).
- **`refresh` support is read off `auth[0]`** unconditionally in `packages/server/api/src/app/app-connection/app-connection-service/app-connection.handler.ts`, so a `refresh` declared on a later entry is never detected.

## Why it is hard to avoid

Only `CUSTOM_AUTH` and `OIDC` accept arbitrary fields. `SecretText` and `BasicAuth` take no extra field, so **any method that needs its own URL must be a `CustomAuth`** — which makes this bite precisely the self-hosted pieces, where each method needs an instance URL alongside the credentials.

Umami avoids it only by coincidence: its split is cloud (fixed URL → `SecretText`) vs self-hosted (`CustomAuth`), so the URL falls on one side. A piece whose methods split by *credential kind* rather than by *hosting* has no such escape.

`OIDC` technically accepts free-form props, but it means OpenID Connect identity federation (used by the AWS pieces for assume-role, with a server-signed key) — using it as a second `CustomAuth` slot would misrepresent the connection type in the database.

## The workaround, and what it costs

The current fallback is a single `CustomAuth` holding every field from both methods, plus a `StaticDropdown` to name the intent and MarkDown blocks telling users to leave the other section blank — see `packages/pieces/community/baserow/src/lib/auth.ts`.

It cannot be improved, because `CustomAuthProps` only accepts static properties (no `DynamicProperties`, no `refreshers`), so there is no way to show or hide fields based on the dropdown. Every user sees every field of both methods on one page, and the dropdown is read only at runtime — the UI ignores it.

## This has already cost the project

- #12226 (merged 8 Apr) shipped Baserow with `baserowAuth = [databaseTokenAuth, jwtAuth]` — two `CustomAuth`.
- #12504 was opened 9 Apr, the day after, following that pattern for Postiz.
- #12759 (23 Apr) removed JWT auth from Baserow entirely; the array form did not work.
- #12964 (29 Apr) restored it as the single-`CustomAuth`-plus-dropdown workaround above.
- #12504 was closed 2 Jun: *"Multiple auths of the same type (`CustomAuth`) are not supported in a piece."* Correct — but the pattern it used was in `main` when it was written, and the replacement pattern had landed five weeks earlier.

Since nothing enforces the constraint, the next piece author will reach for the array form the same way.

## Proposed direction

Give auth properties an explicit discriminator (e.g. an `id`), persist it on the connection, and resolve through it in `getAuthPropertyForValue`, falling back to the current type matching when absent. That is the smallest change that makes the existing multi-auth mechanism actually general, rather than adding a second mechanism alongside it.

Two things to settle before implementing:

- **Migration of existing connections.** #14992 already reports that changing a piece's declared auth silently breaks connections created under the old shape — the same machinery, so the two should be designed together.
- **Whether to instead reject duplicate types at metadata validation**, as a cheap first step, so the failure is loud at build time instead of silent at connection time.

Happy to implement this — raising it first so the direction can be agreed before any code, given it touches the framework, the engine, the server and the web app.

issue.title: [BUG]: formula fails with "Invalid formula" when a bare text argument contains an apostrophe (don't, O'Brien)
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
A formula whose **bare (unquoted) text argument** contains an apostrophe fails the step with `Invalid formula — check for empty values or mismatched parentheses`. Bare text arguments are documented and tested (`uppercase(hello)`, `if_null({{val}};N/A)`), so contractions and names like O'Brien in a typed argument break a flow at run time.

Root cause, in `packages/core/formula/src/lib/formula-evaluator.ts` (main @ d2b0b09669):
- `findMatchingParen` (L406-425), `splitArgsBySemicolon` (L358) and `replaceInlineJsonArrays` (L125) treat every `'` as the start of a single-quoted string.
- In `uppercase(don't stop)`, the apostrophe opens a "string" that never closes. `findMatchingParen` returns -1, the call is never auto-quoted, and expr-eval rejects the expression.

The engine evaluates this for every step input that contains a formula (`packages/server/engine/src/lib/variables/props-resolver.ts` → `formulaEvaluator.evaluate`) and throws `FormulaEvaluationError`, which fails the step.

**To Reproduce**
1. In any step input, use the formula `uppercase(don't stop)`, or `if_empty({{name}};Mr. O'Brien)` with an empty `name`.
2. Run the flow. The step fails with `Invalid formula — …`.

Failing tests in `packages/core/shared/test/formula/function-evaluator.test.ts` ("implicit string quoting"). 3 are red on main with `{ result: null, error: 'Invalid formula — …' }`:

```ts
expect(ok("uppercase(don't stop)")).toEqual({ result: "DON'T STOP", error: null })
expect(result("if_empty({{name}};Mr. O'Brien)", { name: '' })).toBe("Mr. O'Brien")
expect(result("replace({{text}};don't;do not)", { text: "I don't know" })).toBe('I do not know')
```

**Expected behavior**
An apostrophe inside a bare word is text. Only a `'` that starts an argument opens a single-quoted string, so `combine('a;b';c;-)` keeps working.

**Additional context**
A fix with regression tests is ready on [breken-ai/activepieces `fix/formula-apostrophe-in-bare-text`](https://github.com/breken-ai/activepieces/tree/fix/formula-apostrophe-in-bare-text). The formula suite passes (263/263), and `tsc` and eslint on `packages/core/formula` are clean.

I know unsolicited external PRs are paused, so I haven't opened one. If you'd like it, add `keep-open` or take the branch as is. The web tokenizer (`text-input-utils.ts`) has the same `'` rule when it re-renders a saved formula.

issue.title: [BUG]: MCP OAuth access tokens use hardcoded iss "activepieces", not the issuer advertised in OAuth metadata
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**

MCP OAuth access tokens are signed with `iss: "activepieces"` (hardcoded), while the
authorization server metadata advertises the issuer as the public URL derived from the
request (e.g. `http://<host>`). Clients and gateways that validate the `iss` claim of JWT
access tokens against the advertised issuer (e.g. IBM ContextForge MCP Gateway) reject
these tokens, so the Activepieces MCP server cannot be used behind them.

Environment:
- Self-hosted, Docker, single container, fresh database. `AP_FRONTEND_URL` set and present
  in the API process environment.
- Reproduced on **0.92.1** (latest release at the time of writing) and on 0.85.4.
- Reproduced without any third-party client (plain authorization code + PKCE flow with curl).

**To Reproduce**

1. `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` → `"issuer": "http://<host>"`
2. `POST /register` a public client (`token_endpoint_auth_method: none`,
   redirect URI `http://localhost:9999/callback`).
3. Open `/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=…&code_challenge=…&code_challenge_method=S256&scope=mcp&resource=http://<host>/mcp/platform` and approve.
4. `POST /token` with `grant_type=authorization_code`, `code`, `client_id`, `code_verifier`, `redirect_uri`.
5. Decode the access token payload (identifiers redacted):

```json
{
  "type": "mcp_oauth",
  "scopes": ["mcp"],
  "aud": "MCP_OAUTH_ACCESS",
  "iss": "activepieces",
  "exp": "<iat + 900>"
}
```

**Expected behavior**

The `iss` claim of the access token equals the `issuer` advertised in the authorization
server metadata (RFC 8414 §3.3; RFC 9068 §2.2 for JWT access tokens).

**Root cause (from the source code)**

- Metadata issuer: `domainHelper.getPublicUrlFromRequest({ req })` in
  `packages/server/api/src/app/mcp/oauth/metadata/mcp-oauth-metadata.controller.ts`.
- Token issuer: `const ISSUER = 'activepieces'` in `packages/server/api/src/app/helper/jwt-utils.ts`.
  - 0.85.x: `sign()` hardcodes `issuer: ISSUER` and takes no issuer parameter.
  - `main`: `sign()` accepts `issuer` (`issuer ?? ISSUER`), but `issueAccessToken()` in
    `packages/server/api/src/app/mcp/oauth/token/mcp-oauth-token.service.ts` does not pass it.
- `verifyAccessToken()` verifies with the default `ISSUER`, so a token carrying the URL
  issuer would currently be rejected by Activepieces itself.

**Suggested fix**

For `MCP_OAUTH_ACCESS` tokens, use the same public URL as the metadata `issuer` when signing
(`issueAccessToken`) and when verifying (`verifyAccessToken`). Other internal JWT types can
keep the current constant. Since the metadata issuer is request-derived, signing and
verification should use the same derivation (or a configured canonical public URL), so tokens
keep working when the instance is reachable under several hostnames.

**Additional context**

Minor, related observations:
- `aud` is the constant `MCP_OAUTH_ACCESS` rather than the RFC 8707 `resource` sent by the client.
- With a non-default port in the public URL (e.g. `http://host:8085`), the published metadata
  URLs drop the port (the metadata issuer is derived from the request base URL).

Note: in plain OAuth 2.0, access tokens are opaque to clients, so this mainly affects clients
or gateways that validate JWT claims before forwarding tokens. The inconsistency between the
metadata issuer and the token `iss` is still what such clients detect.

Related: #13596 / #13603 and #15376 changed how the **metadata** issuer is derived
(base path, `AP_MCP_URL`), but neither touches the token `iss`
(`jwt-utils.ts` / `mcp-oauth-token.service.ts`), so the mismatch remains on 0.92.1.

issue.title: [BUG]: formula fails with "Invalid formula" when a bare text argument contains an apostrophe (don't, O'Brien)
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
A formula whose **bare (unquoted) text argument** contains an apostrophe fails the step with `Invalid formula — check for empty values or mismatched parentheses`. Bare text arguments are documented and tested (`uppercase(hello)`, `if_null({{val}};N/A)`), so contractions and names like O'Brien in a typed argument break a flow at run time.

Root cause, in `packages/core/formula/src/lib/formula-evaluator.ts` (main @ d2b0b09669):
- `findMatchingParen` (L406-425), `splitArgsBySemicolon` (L358) and `replaceInlineJsonArrays` (L125) treat every `'` as the start of a single-quoted string.
- In `uppercase(don't stop)`, the apostrophe opens a "string" that never closes. `findMatchingParen` returns -1, the call is never auto-quoted, and expr-eval rejects the expression.

The engine evaluates this for every step input that contains a formula (`packages/server/engine/src/lib/variables/props-resolver.ts` → `formulaEvaluator.evaluate`) and throws `FormulaEvaluationError`, which fails the step.

**To Reproduce**
1. In any step input, use the formula `uppercase(don't stop)`, or `if_empty({{name}};Mr. O'Brien)` with an empty `name`.
2. Run the flow. The step fails with `Invalid formula — …`.

Failing tests in `packages/core/shared/test/formula/function-evaluator.test.ts` ("implicit string quoting"). 3 are red on main with `{ result: null, error: 'Invalid formula — …' }`:

```ts
expect(ok("uppercase(don't stop)")).toEqual({ result: "DON'T STOP", error: null })
expect(result("if_empty({{name}};Mr. O'Brien)", { name: '' })).toBe("Mr. O'Brien")
expect(result("replace({{text}};don't;do not)", { text: "I don't know" })).toBe('I do not know')
```

**Expected behavior**
An apostrophe inside a bare word is text. Only a `'` that starts an argument opens a single-quoted string, so `combine('a;b';c;-)` keeps working.

**Additional context**
A fix with regression tests is ready on [breken-ai/activepieces `fix/formula-apostrophe-in-bare-text`](https://github.com/breken-ai/activepieces/tree/fix/formula-apostrophe-in-bare-text). The formula suite passes (263/263), and `tsc` and eslint on `packages/core/formula` are clean.

I know unsolicited external PRs are paused, so I haven't opened one. If you'd like it, add `keep-open` or take the branch as is. The web tokenizer (`text-input-utils.ts`) has the same `'` rule when it re-renders a saved formula.

_Prepared with AI assistance (Claude) from the breken-ai account._

issue.title: [BUG]: MCP OAuth access tokens use hardcoded iss "activepieces", not the issuer advertised in OAuth metadata
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**

MCP OAuth access tokens are signed with `iss: "activepieces"` (hardcoded), while the
authorization server metadata advertises the issuer as the public URL derived from the
request (e.g. `http://<host>`). Clients and gateways that validate the `iss` claim of JWT
access tokens against the advertised issuer (e.g. IBM ContextForge MCP Gateway) reject
these tokens, so the Activepieces MCP server cannot be used behind them.

Environment:
- Self-hosted, Docker, single container, fresh database. `AP_FRONTEND_URL` set and present
  in the API process environment.
- Reproduced on **0.92.1** (latest release at the time of writing) and on 0.85.4.
- Reproduced without any third-party client (plain authorization code + PKCE flow with curl).

**To Reproduce**

1. `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` → `"issuer": "http://<host>"`
2. `POST /register` a public client (`token_endpoint_auth_method: none`,
   redirect URI `http://localhost:9999/callback`).
3. Open `/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=…&code_challenge=…&code_challenge_method=S256&scope=mcp&resource=http://<host>/mcp/platform` and approve.
4. `POST /token` with `grant_type=authorization_code`, `code`, `client_id`, `code_verifier`, `redirect_uri`.
5. Decode the access token payload (identifiers redacted):

```json
{
  "type": "mcp_oauth",
  "scopes": ["mcp"],
  "aud": "MCP_OAUTH_ACCESS",
  "iss": "activepieces",
  "exp": "<iat + 900>"
}
```

**Expected behavior**

The `iss` claim of the access token equals the `issuer` advertised in the authorization
server metadata (RFC 8414 §3.3; RFC 9068 §2.2 for JWT access tokens).

**Root cause (from the source code)**

- Metadata issuer: `domainHelper.getPublicUrlFromRequest({ req })` in
  `packages/server/api/src/app/mcp/oauth/metadata/mcp-oauth-metadata.controller.ts`.
- Token issuer: `const ISSUER = 'activepieces'` in `packages/server/api/src/app/helper/jwt-utils.ts`.
  - 0.85.x: `sign()` hardcodes `issuer: ISSUER` and takes no issuer parameter.
  - `main`: `sign()` accepts `issuer` (`issuer ?? ISSUER`), but `issueAccessToken()` in
    `packages/server/api/src/app/mcp/oauth/token/mcp-oauth-token.service.ts` does not pass it.
- `verifyAccessToken()` verifies with the default `ISSUER`, so a token carrying the URL
  issuer would currently be rejected by Activepieces itself.

**Suggested fix**

For `MCP_OAUTH_ACCESS` tokens, use the same public URL as the metadata `issuer` when signing
(`issueAccessToken`) and when verifying (`verifyAccessToken`). Other internal JWT types can
keep the current constant. Since the metadata issuer is request-derived, signing and
verification should use the same derivation (or a configured canonical public URL), so tokens
keep working when the instance is reachable under several hostnames.

**Additional context**

Minor, related observations:
- `aud` is the constant `MCP_OAUTH_ACCESS` rather than the RFC 8707 `resource` sent by the client.
- With a non-default port in the public URL (e.g. `http://host:8085`), the published metadata
  URLs drop the port (the metadata issuer is derived from the request base URL).

Note: in plain OAuth 2.0, access tokens are opaque to clients, so this mainly affects clients
or gateways that validate JWT claims before forwarding tokens. The inconsistency between the
metadata issuer and the token `iss` is still what such clients detect.

Related: #13596 / #13603 and #15376 changed how the **metadata** issuer is derived
(base path, `AP_MCP_URL`), but neither touches the token `iss`
(`jwt-utils.ts` / `mcp-oauth-token.service.ts`), so the mismatch remains on 0.92.1.

issue.title: Project variable Copy reference is flagged as missing by flow validator
issue.body:
Environment

- Activepieces Cloud, Personal Project. The exact cloud version is unavailable in the read-only UI.
- Webhook trigger: "@activepieces/piece-webhook" v0.1.42.
- HTTP action: "@activepieces/piece-http" v0.12.1.
- The draft flow is disabled and unpublished.

Observed behavior

A project variable exists in the same visible project as the draft flow. Its Copy reference text matches the reference in an HTTP action JSON body. With the variable name replaced for privacy, the expression has this form: "{{variables['EXAMPLE_SECRET']}}". The "Project Variables guide" (https://www.activepieces.com/docs/flows/project-variables) documents this syntax.

Read-only structural validation reports a "template_reference" error on the HTTP action, saying the "{{variables...}}" reference does not exist in the flow. It reports 14 structurally valid steps and no invalid steps, but "valid=false" overall because of this error. The variable value was not revealed.

Expected behavior / clarification requested

Does the flow validator resolve project-scoped variables, or does it validate only step-output references? If this expression is valid at runtime but cannot be resolved by the validator, please document that distinction. If the error indicates a scope or permission problem, please explain how to diagnose it without revealing the value or running or publishing the flow.

Reproduction information available

1. In one Personal Project, create a project variable and copy its reference from the Variables page.
2. Insert the exact reference into an HTTP action JSON input of a disabled, unpublished draft flow.
3. Run structural validation only, without running the flow.
4. Observe a "template_reference" error for "{{variables...}}".

This describes the observed configuration; I have not independently reproduced it in a fresh project. The webhook Header Auth fields also appear empty. That is a separate incomplete configuration. Please distinguish it from the variable-reference validation error.

issue.title: [BUG]: Failed table deletions can send later edits to the wrong record or field
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**

A failed row or column deletion can leave the Tables editor displaying a different positional layout from the layout used to build later API requests. An ordinary cell edit then targets a valid but unintended record or field. The request can succeed, making this a data-integrity problem rather than only a missing error notification.

For example, after a failed deletion of Alice, Bob becomes the first visible row. Editing Bob to Robert sends the update to Alice's record ID. After a failed deletion of the Name column, Email becomes the first visible column, but editing that Email cell sends the value with the Name field ID.

The failure requires only one rejected DELETE followed by another edit in the same editor session. It does not require two editors, an import, malformed data, or special permissions. An edit already queued while the DELETE is pending is also exposed: when the DELETE rejects, the next queued operation proceeds using positions from the optimistic view.

This report is based on upstream commit [`518ae7091c35fe0a5035b987e3cffd0b8c007133`](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/tree/518ae7091c35fe0a5035b987e3cffd0b8c007133). The outbound mutation mismatch was reproduced by executing the actual client store, server mirror, and queue with controlled API failures. The API boundaries were substituted; the state and queue implementations were not.

**To Reproduce**

Use a disposable table and intercept only the indicated DELETE request. Return HTTP 500 before applying the deletion, or reject the request before it reaches the server. Allow subsequent POST requests normally. A blanket offline setting is less useful because it prevents observing the incorrectly addressed update.

### Row deletion

1. Create a table with two text fields, Name and Email, and these records in order:

   | Name | Email |
   | --- | --- |
   | Alice | alice@example.com |
   | Bob | bob@example.com |

2. Record Alice's and Bob's actual record IDs from the records response. The names `alice-id` and `bob-id` below are illustrative IDs, not assumed generated values.
3. Select Alice and confirm **Delete Records**.
4. Make that `DELETE /api/v1/records/` request fail without deleting Alice on the server. Leave other requests unaffected.
5. Alice disappears from the local grid because the client removes the row optimistically. Bob now occupies visible row index 0.
6. Change Bob's visible Name cell from Bob to Robert.
7. Inspect the resulting record-update POST. Its URL contains Alice's ID, even though the edited visible row is Bob:

   ```text
   POST /api/v1/records/alice-id
   ```

   The cells payload contains the Name field ID and the value `Robert`.
8. If the normal update endpoint accepts the request, reloading the table exposes the unintended overwrite: Alice's Name has become Robert while Bob remains Bob.

The state-level reproduction verifies the incorrectly addressed outbound request in step 7. The unintended stored change follows if the normal update endpoint accepts that request, as described in step 8.

### Column deletion

1. Restore the original two-column table.
2. Record the actual Name and Email field IDs.
3. Delete the Name field through its field action menu.
4. Make only `DELETE /api/v1/fields/<name-field-id>` fail before the server removes the field.
5. Email remains visible and has moved to client field index 0.
6. Edit Alice's visible Email cell to `alice+updated@example.com`.
7. Inspect the record-update payload. Its `fieldId` is the Name field ID rather than the Email field ID:

   ```json
   {
     "tableId": "<table-id>",
     "cells": [
       {
         "fieldId": "<name-field-id>",
         "value": "alice+updated@example.com"
       }
     ]
   }
   ```

Both variants can also be reproduced by delaying the intercepted DELETE, making a cell edit while it is pending, and then rejecting it. The queued edit must be treated as dependent on the deletion's outcome, not as an independently safe request.

**Expected behavior**

A rejected table mutation must not allow later positional operations to write to another logical record or field. The editor should explain that saving failed and require a safe recovery before accepting additional edits.

Recovery must reload the table metadata, fields, and records together and rebuild both mirrors only after all required fetches succeed. If a reload fails, editing must remain blocked. A later successful background refetch of only the records must not silently reset the failure state or enable writes against partially refreshed data.

When deletion succeeds, normal editing should continue: deleting Alice must make a following edit target Bob, and deleting a field must retain the surviving cell values and correctly resolve their shifted field IDs.

**Additional context**

### Root cause

The editor maintains an optimistic client layout and a separate server mirror. Later mutations carry positional indexes into the server mirror, which resolves them to persistent IDs when the queued operation executes.

The client [filters selected records immediately](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/blob/518ae7091c35fe0a5035b987e3cffd0b8c007133/packages/web/src/features/tables/stores/store/ap-tables-client-state.tsx#L193-L201), while server-side [record removal occurs only after the DELETE resolves](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/blob/518ae7091c35fe0a5035b987e3cffd0b8c007133/packages/web/src/features/tables/stores/store/ap-tables-server-state.ts#L94-L112). A rejection therefore leaves Bob at client index 0 and Alice at server-mirror index 0.

The same divergence occurs for fields: the client [removes the field and renumbers surviving cells](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/blob/518ae7091c35fe0a5035b987e3cffd0b8c007133/packages/web/src/features/tables/stores/store/ap-tables-client-state.tsx#L222-L240), while the mirror [awaits the API deletion before removing the field](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/blob/518ae7091c35fe0a5035b987e3cffd0b8c007133/packages/web/src/features/tables/stores/store/ap-tables-server-state.ts#L37-L49).

A later [update resolves both indexes through the unchanged mirror](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/blob/518ae7091c35fe0a5035b987e3cffd0b8c007133/packages/web/src/features/tables/stores/store/ap-tables-server-state.ts#L77-L91). The IDs can still be valid, so ordinary API validation cannot determine that the user meant the newly displayed row or column.

The table's [queue wrapper has no failure recovery](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/blob/518ae7091c35fe0a5035b987e3cffd0b8c007133/packages/web/src/features/tables/stores/store/ap-tables-server-state.ts#L29-L35). The [shared queue executes each callback under a mutex](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/blob/518ae7091c35fe0a5035b987e3cffd0b8c007133/packages/web/src/lib/promise-queue.ts#L20-L27); rejection releases the mutex, allowing subsequent callbacks to execute unless the queue is explicitly halted.

A normal query refresh is not enough by itself: the provider [retains its store in a ref](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/blob/518ae7091c35fe0a5035b987e3cffd0b8c007133/packages/web/src/features/tables/components/ap-table-state-provider.tsx#L35-L53). Its [explicit refresh path uses a remount key](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/blob/518ae7091c35fe0a5035b987e3cffd0b8c007133/packages/web/src/features/tables/components/ap-table-state-provider.tsx#L113-L123) to rebuild the store.

### Suggested repair and acceptance criteria

Catch failures at the Tables mutation queue boundary, halt that table's queue before dependent callbacks run, expose a save-error state, and replace the editor with an explanation and a reload action. Pending positional writes should not be replayed automatically. A network error may leave the outcome of the failed request uncertain, so fetching authoritative state is safer than assuming rollback or retrying deletion.

Regression coverage should connect the real client store, server mirror, and queue. It should verify zero update requests after failed row and field deletions, including already queued edits; correct IDs after successful deletions; retained values after a successful middle-field deletion; and recovery that remains blocked until a complete explicit reload succeeds. The existing successful column-remapping fix addresses a different path: successful renumbering does not prevent the two mirrors from diverging when the API deletion rejects.


### Fix prepared

The accompanying patch handles rejected mutations at the table's queue boundary, stops all dependent writes, and replaces the editor with an explanation and a Reload table action. Reload fetches the table, fields, and records together and creates a new store only when all three requests succeed. A partial or background refresh preserves the halted store. This lets the editor recover from either an unapplied deletion or a deletion whose successful response was lost, without guessing which optimistic edits should be replayed.

The focused store/provider suite passes 9 tests. It confirms that queued and later edits produce no update after a rejected deletion, that successful row and middle-field deletions still address the intended entities, and that editing resumes only after a complete reload.

The fix is implemented on [`fix/tables-delete-failure-integrity`](https://github.com/dakjdakd/activepieces/tree/fix/tables-delete-failure-integrity). The corresponding changes and regression tests are in [PR #16344](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/pull/16344).

issue.title: [BUG]: Polling trigger test samples are listed in reverse order (oldest first)
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
When testing a polling trigger in the builder, the samples are shown in the reverse of the order the trigger's `test()` returned them. Most triggers return newest-first (including `pollingHelper.test`), so the builder shows the **oldest** sample on top and the newest at the bottom. Users testing "did my new email/row arrive?" conclude it is missing.

Cause: `triggerEventService.test` (`packages/server/api/src/app/trigger/trigger-events/trigger-event.service.ts`) saves each output with sequential `await this.saveEvent(...)` calls in the order returned, then returns `this.list(...)`, which orders by `created` `DESC`. The last-saved item (the oldest) comes back first.

**To Reproduce**
1. Add a polling trigger whose `test()` returns newest-first, e.g. Microsoft Outlook **New Email** or any `pollingHelper` TIMEBASED trigger.
2. Click **Test trigger**.
3. The first sample is the oldest of the returned items; the newest is last.

Verified against a local dev stack: the piece returned `[newest, ..., oldest]`, the saved events had ascending `created` timestamps in that order, and `/test-trigger` returned `[oldest, ..., newest]`.

**Expected behavior**
Samples appear in the order the trigger returned them, so the newest item is on top.

**Additional context**
Fix options: save the outputs in reverse order, or have `list` order by `created` ascending for this response.

PR #16108 (Microsoft Outlook New Attachment) works around this by returning `attachments.reverse()` from its `test()`. When this is fixed platform-side, remove that `.reverse()` in the same change, or that trigger's samples will flip back.

issue.title: Impact → Details: Search flows and Download button aren't aligned with the table
issue.body: ## What's wrong On **Impact → Details**, the toolbar row (Search flows, Total Time Saved, Owner, Download) has no horizontal padding. issue.title: [BUG]: Admin run retry ignores required date range
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
The internal admin retry endpoint does not apply its required createdAfter and createdBefore filters. Date-only retries select no runs, while retries with explicit run IDs can include runs outside the requested window.

**To Reproduce**
1. Call POST /v1/admin/platforms/runs/retry with valid createdAfter and createdBefore values and omit runIds.
2. Observe that no runs are retried because the query starts with an empty IN condition.
3. Call the endpoint with run IDs containing a run outside the date window.
4. Observe that the out-of-window run is retried because the date predicates are skipped.

**Expected behavior**
The required date range is always applied. When runIds is omitted, every run in the date window is eligible. When IDs are supplied, the query intersects those IDs with the date window.

**Additional context**
The inverted guards are in adminPlatformService.retryRuns. Add regression coverage for date-only retries and for explicit IDs combined with date bounds.

issue.title: [BUG]: Failed table deletions can send later edits to the wrong record or field
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**

A failed row or column deletion can leave the Tables editor displaying a different positional layout from the layout used to build later API requests. An ordinary cell edit then targets a valid but unintended record or field. The request can succeed, making this a data-integrity problem rather than only a missing error notification.

For example, after a failed deletion of Alice, Bob becomes the first visible row. Editing Bob to Robert sends the update to Alice's record ID. After a failed deletion of the Name column, Email becomes the first visible column, but editing that Email cell sends the value with the Name field ID.

The failure requires only one rejected DELETE followed by another edit in the same editor session. It does not require two editors, an import, malformed data, or special permissions. An edit already queued while the DELETE is pending is also exposed: when the DELETE rejects, the next queued operation proceeds using positions from the optimistic view.

This report is based on upstream commit [`518ae7091c35fe0a5035b987e3cffd0b8c007133`](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/tree/518ae7091c35fe0a5035b987e3cffd0b8c007133). The outbound mutation mismatch was reproduced by executing the actual client store, server mirror, and queue with controlled API failures. The API boundaries were substituted; the state and queue implementations were not.

**To Reproduce**

Use a disposable table and intercept only the indicated DELETE request. Return HTTP 500 before applying the deletion, or reject the request before it reaches the server. Allow subsequent POST requests normally. A blanket offline setting is less useful because it prevents observing the incorrectly addressed update.

### Row deletion

1. Create a table with two text fields, Name and Email, and these records in order:

   | Name | Email |
   | --- | --- |
   | Alice | alice@example.com |
   | Bob | bob@example.com |

2. Record Alice's and Bob's actual record IDs from the records response. The names `alice-id` and `bob-id` below are illustrative IDs, not assumed generated values.
3. Select Alice and confirm **Delete Records**.
4. Make that `DELETE /api/v1/records/` request fail without deleting Alice on the server. Leave other requests unaffected.
5. Alice disappears from the local grid because the client removes the row optimistically. Bob now occupies visible row index 0.
6. Change Bob's visible Name cell from Bob to Robert.
7. Inspect the resulting record-update POST. Its URL contains Alice's ID, even though the edited visible row is Bob:

   ```text
   POST /api/v1/records/alice-id
   ```

   The cells payload contains the Name field ID and the value `Robert`.
8. If the normal update endpoint accepts the request, reloading the table exposes the unintended overwrite: Alice's Name has become Robert while Bob remains Bob.

The state-level reproduction verifies the incorrectly addressed outbound request in step 7. The unintended stored change follows if the normal update endpoint accepts that request, as described in step 8.

### Column deletion

1. Restore the original two-column table.
2. Record the actual Name and Email field IDs.
3. Delete the Name field through its field action menu.
4. Make only `DELETE /api/v1/fields/<name-field-id>` fail before the server removes the field.
5. Email remains visible and has moved to client field index 0.
6. Edit Alice's visible Email cell to `alice+updated@example.com`.
7. Inspect the record-update payload. Its `fieldId` is the Name field ID rather than the Email field ID:

   ```json
   {
     "tableId": "<table-id>",
     "cells": [
       {
         "fieldId": "<name-field-id>",
         "value": "alice+updated@example.com"
       }
     ]
   }
   ```

Both variants can also be reproduced by delaying the intercepted DELETE, making a cell edit while it is pending, and then rejecting it. The queued edit must be treated as dependent on the deletion's outcome, not as an independently safe request.

**Expected behavior**

A rejected table mutation must not allow later positional operations to write to another logical record or field. The editor should explain that saving failed and require a safe recovery before accepting additional edits.

Recovery must reload the table metadata, fields, and records together and rebuild both mirrors only after all required fetches succeed. If a reload fails, editing must remain blocked. A later successful background refetch of only the records must not silently reset the failure state or enable writes against partially refreshed data.

When deletion succeeds, normal editing should continue: deleting Alice must make a following edit target Bob, and deleting a field must retain the surviving cell values and correctly resolve their shifted field IDs.

**Additional context**

### Root cause

The editor maintains an optimistic client layout and a separate server mirror. Later mutations carry positional indexes into the server mirror, which resolves them to persistent IDs when the queued operation executes.

The client [filters selected records immediately](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/blob/518ae7091c35fe0a5035b987e3cffd0b8c007133/packages/web/src/features/tables/stores/store/ap-tables-client-state.tsx#L193-L201), while server-side [record removal occurs only after the DELETE resolves](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/blob/518ae7091c35fe0a5035b987e3cffd0b8c007133/packages/web/src/features/tables/stores/store/ap-tables-server-state.ts#L94-L112). A rejection therefore leaves Bob at client index 0 and Alice at server-mirror index 0.

The same divergence occurs for fields: the client [removes the field and renumbers surviving cells](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/blob/518ae7091c35fe0a5035b987e3cffd0b8c007133/packages/web/src/features/tables/stores/store/ap-tables-client-state.tsx#L222-L240), while the mirror [awaits the API deletion before removing the field](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/blob/518ae7091c35fe0a5035b987e3cffd0b8c007133/packages/web/src/features/tables/stores/store/ap-tables-server-state.ts#L37-L49).

A later [update resolves both indexes through the unchanged mirror](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/blob/518ae7091c35fe0a5035b987e3cffd0b8c007133/packages/web/src/features/tables/stores/store/ap-tables-server-state.ts#L77-L91). The IDs can still be valid, so ordinary API validation cannot determine that the user meant the newly displayed row or column.

The table's [queue wrapper has no failure recovery](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/blob/518ae7091c35fe0a5035b987e3cffd0b8c007133/packages/web/src/features/tables/stores/store/ap-tables-server-state.ts#L29-L35). The [shared queue executes each callback under a mutex](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/blob/518ae7091c35fe0a5035b987e3cffd0b8c007133/packages/web/src/lib/promise-queue.ts#L20-L27); rejection releases the mutex, allowing subsequent callbacks to execute unless the queue is explicitly halted.

A normal query refresh is not enough by itself: the provider [retains its store in a ref](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/blob/518ae7091c35fe0a5035b987e3cffd0b8c007133/packages/web/src/features/tables/components/ap-table-state-provider.tsx#L35-L53). Its [explicit refresh path uses a remount key](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/blob/518ae7091c35fe0a5035b987e3cffd0b8c007133/packages/web/src/features/tables/components/ap-table-state-provider.tsx#L113-L123) to rebuild the store.

### Suggested repair and acceptance criteria

Catch failures at the Tables mutation queue boundary, halt that table's queue before dependent callbacks run, expose a save-error state, and replace the editor with an explanation and a reload action. Pending positional writes should not be replayed automatically. A network error may leave the outcome of the failed request uncertain, so fetching authoritative state is safer than assuming rollback or retrying deletion.

Regression coverage should connect the real client store, server mirror, and queue. It should verify zero update requests after failed row and field deletions, including already queued edits; correct IDs after successful deletions; retained values after a successful middle-field deletion; and recovery that remains blocked until a complete explicit reload succeeds. The existing successful column-remapping fix addresses a different path: successful renumbering does not prevent the two mirrors from diverging when the API deletion rejects.


### Fix prepared

The accompanying patch handles rejected mutations at the table's queue boundary, stops all dependent writes, and replaces the editor with an explanation and a Reload table action. Reload fetches the table, fields, and records together and creates a new store only when all three requests succeed. A partial or background refresh preserves the halted store. This lets the editor recover from either an unapplied deletion or a deletion whose successful response was lost, without guessing which optimistic edits should be replayed.

The focused store/provider suite passes 9 tests. It confirms that queued and later edits produce no update after a rejected deletion, that successful row and middle-field deletions still address the intended entities, and that editing resumes only after a complete reload.

The fix is implemented on [`fix/tables-delete-failure-integrity`](https://github.com/dakjdakd/activepieces/tree/fix/tables-delete-failure-integrity). The corresponding changes and regression tests are in [PR #16344](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/pull/16344).

issue.title: Activepieces Cloud Validator falsely flags Project Variable references in nine HTTP steps — GitHub Issue #15853
issue.body:
**Subject:** Activepieces Cloud Validator falsely flags Project Variable references in nine HTTP steps — GitHub Issue #15853

**Environment**
- Activepieces Cloud — Personal Project
- Main Flow ID: 
- Flow state: Disabled / Unpublished
- Related issue: https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/issues/15853

**Problem**

The Main Flow validator reports nine `template_reference` errors for the documented Project Variable reference:

`{{variables['ATOMIC_CLAIM_API_TOKEN']}}`

Affected steps:
- Claim Requests: `step_33`, `step_35`, `step_37`
- RECORD_RESULT Requests: `step_40`, `step_43`, `step_44`
- Failure Recorders: `step_45`, `step_47`, `step_49`

The validator reports that `variables...` does not exist in the flow, although this is a project-scoped variable reference.

**Evidence**
- The same reference succeeded in an isolated Activepieces Runtime Mock Test.
- The Main Flow validator still returns `valid:false` because of these nine reference errors.
- No secret value is included in this report.
- No production run or publication was performed to reproduce the issue.

**Expected behavior**

The validator should recognize documented project-scoped variable references, or clearly distinguish unresolved project variables from missing step-output references.

**Questions**
1. Is this a known validator defect corresponding to GitHub Issue #15853?
2. Is there an official workaround or confirmed fix available for Activepieces Cloud?
3. Can the validator be corrected without changing the documented reference or exposing/replacing the secret?
4. Can Support confirm whether these errors block publishing, without publishing or enabling this flow?

Please advise on a supported resolution. The flow must remain disabled and unpublished while this is investigated.

issue.title: Release Pieces: wait for the npm tarball before inserting piece metadata
issue.body:
## Problem

`release-pieces.yml` runs "update pieces metadata" as soon as `npm publish` succeeds. npm lists a new version straight away, but its tarball can take a few minutes to become downloadable. During that gap cloud shows the new version, and every step that uses it fails with:

```json
{"code":"ENGINE_OPERATION_FAILURE","params":{"message":"PIECE_BUNDLE_NOT_AVAILABLE","context":{"status":"INTERNAL_ERROR"}}}
```

The bundle isn't on cdn.activepieces.com either, so `pieceBundle.resolve` redirects the worker to the npm tarball. npm returns 404, and the sandbox's `downloadBundleIfNotCached` reports `PIECE_BUNDLE_NOT_AVAILABLE`.

## Seen on

`@activepieces/piece-microsoft-365-planner@0.4.0` (#16720), 2026-10-21, UTC:

- 13:52:28: metadata inserted on cloud (run 39611516917); the version shows in the builder.
- 13:54:25: npm records the publish.
- until 13:58:22: `https://registry.npmjs.org/@activepieces/piece-microsoft-365-planner/-/piece-microsoft-365-planner-0.4.0.tgz` returns `404 {"error":"Not found"}`; the dropdown (`POST /v1/pieces/options`) fails.
- from 13:58:22: the tarball returns 200 and the step works, with no restart or cache clear.

npm doesn't guarantee that a version is downloadable as soon as it's listed. Usually the gap is seconds; this one was about 4 minutes.

## Proposed fix

Gate each piece's metadata insert on its own tarball being downloadable:

- For each piece published in the run, send a `HEAD` request to its npm tarball URL (status only, no download) every 10 s until it returns 200.
- Check in parallel batches of about 20, the same batching `update-pieces-metadata.ts` already uses, so a bulk release takes about as long as its slowest tarball rather than the sum (around 15 s for 300 pieces when every tarball is ready).
- Insert each piece's metadata as soon as its own tarball returns 200, so one slow piece doesn't hold back the rest.
- If a piece's tarball still isn't ready after about 10 minutes, skip that piece's metadata, report it in the job log and the Discord failure notice, and let the other pieces go through.

Normally every tarball returns 200 on the first try, so this adds about a second per batch.

issue.body:
Environment

- Activepieces Cloud, Personal Project. The exact cloud version is unavailable in the read-only UI.
- Webhook trigger: "@activepieces/piece-webhook" v0.1.42.
- HTTP action: "@activepieces/piece-http" v0.12.1.
- The draft flow is disabled and unpublished.

Observed behavior

A project variable exists in the same visible project as the draft flow. Its Copy reference text matches the reference in an HTTP action JSON body. issue.title: [BUG]: Admin run retry ignores required date range
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
The internal admin retry endpoint does not apply its required createdAfter and createdBefore filters. Date-only retries select no runs, while retries with explicit run IDs can include runs outside the requested window.

**To Reproduce**
1. Call POST /v1/admin/platforms/runs/retry with valid createdAfter and createdBefore values and omit runIds.
2. Observe that no runs are retried because the query starts with an empty IN condition.
3. Call the endpoint with run IDs containing a run outside the date window.
4. Observe that the out-of-window run is retried because the date predicates are skipped.

**Expected behavior**
The required date range is always applied. When runIds is omitted, every run in the date window is eligible. When IDs are supplied, the query intersects those IDs with the date window.

**Additional context**
The inverted guards are in adminPlatformService.retryRuns. Add regression coverage for date-only retries and for explicit IDs combined with date bounds.

issue.title: [BUG]: Stopping a worker kills any run longer than 25 s, and WORKER_AND_APP containers skip the drain entirely
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**

When a worker receives SIGTERM (a deploy, an autoscaler scaling in, node consolidation), `stop()` waits at most 25 s (`DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS` in `packages/server/worker/src/lib/worker.ts`) for its in-flight jobs, and `main.ts` force-exits at 30 s. Any run longer than that is killed partway through, even when the orchestrator would wait longer, and there is no setting to raise the limit.

In the default `WORKER_AND_APP` container the drain can't finish at all. `docker-entrypoint.sh` sends SIGTERM to the app and the worker at the same moment. The app shuts down without waiting for the worker, and its exit drops the worker's socket. The worker's disconnect handler then aborts the in-flight runtime, and the entrypoint exits as soon as either process has.

Killed runs fall back to the stalled scan. Once a job runs out of stalled attempts, nothing finalizes its `flow_run`, so the run stays `RUNNING` forever. That is #14372, which was closed as not planned. We run self-hosted CE on Kubernetes with KEDA scaling the deployment, and these orphaned runs pile up after every scale-in.

**To Reproduce**

The entrypoint ordering, reproduced with stub app and worker processes under `dash` (the image's `/bin/sh`). Each stub logs when it gets SIGTERM. The stub app exits 0.2 s later; the stub worker "drains" for 3 s. The entrypoint is sent SIGTERM at t = 2 s:

```
current main                          proposed
2.0s worker: got SIGTERM              2.0s worker: got SIGTERM
2.0s app: got SIGTERM                 5.0s worker: exiting
2.2s app: exiting                     5.0s app: got SIGTERM
(entrypoint exits 1 at ~3.0s,         5.2s app: exiting
 worker still draining)               (entrypoint exits 0)
```

**Expected behavior**

A worker that is asked to stop should be allowed to finish its in-flight runs for as long as the operator chooses, up to the flow timeout. In `WORKER_AND_APP` the app should stay up until the worker has drained, because the worker reports its jobs through that app.

**Proposed fix**

Branch: https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/compare/main...SimonRelu:activepieces:fix/worker-graceful-drain (7 files, +105/-10). It isn't a PR because external PRs are auto-closed; we're happy to open one if you add `keep-open`.

- New `AP_WORKER_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default `25`, so nothing changes unless it's set) controls how long `stop()` waits. The force-exit timer in `main.ts` becomes that value plus 5 s. An invalid value falls back to 25 with a warning, and `0` skips the drain.
- `docker-entrypoint.sh` (`WORKER_AND_APP`): on TERM or INT, signal the worker and wait for it to exit, then signal the app and wait for that. A signal-triggered stop now exits 0 instead of 1.
- Adds a row to the environment variable reference and updates the drain note on the workers brain page.
- Tests: `getDrainTimeoutMs` parsing, plus an integration test that `stop()` lets an in-flight job finish and call `completeJob` before disconnecting. Worker suite 40/40, worker lint 0 errors, `tsc --noEmit` clean.

An operator who wants long runs to survive scale-in would set, for example, `AP_WORKER_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=1800` together with `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 1810`.

This covers only graceful stops. Abrupt deaths (OOM, SIGKILL) still need the run reaper proposed in #14372.

issue.title: Updating a missing event destination returns 500 instead of 404
issue.body:
## Bug
Updating an event destination ID that does not exist returns HTTP 500 with an unhandled TypeORM `EntityNotFoundError`. The update should return HTTP 404 with `ENTITY_NOT_FOUND`.

## Reproduction
1. On a platform with Event Streaming enabled, send `POST /api/v1/event-destinations/<valid-but-nonexistent-id>` with a valid update body.
2. Observe HTTP 500.

The existing integration test in `packages/server/api/test/integration/cloud/event-destinations/event-destination.test.ts` documents the current 500 behavior.

## Expected behavior
Return HTTP 404 and the standard `ENTITY_NOT_FOUND` code. Keep the lookup scoped to the platform and inside the transaction so the row lock and header update safeguards continue to apply.

issue.title: Release Pieces: wait for the npm tarball before inserting piece metadata
issue.body:
## Problem

`release-pieces.yml` runs "update pieces metadata" as soon as `npm publish` succeeds. npm lists a new version straight away, but its tarball can take a few minutes to become downloadable. During that gap cloud shows the new version, and every step that uses it fails with:

```json
{"code":"ENGINE_OPERATION_FAILURE","params":{"message":"PIECE_BUNDLE_NOT_AVAILABLE","context":{"status":"INTERNAL_ERROR"}}}
```

The bundle isn't on cdn.activepieces.com either, so `pieceBundle.resolve` redirects the worker to the npm tarball. npm returns 404, and the sandbox's `downloadBundleIfNotCached` reports `PIECE_BUNDLE_NOT_AVAILABLE`.

## Seen on

`@activepieces/piece-microsoft-365-planner@0.4.0` (#16720), 2026-10-21, UTC:

- 13:52:28: metadata inserted on cloud (run 39611516917); the version shows in the builder.
- 13:54:25: npm records the publish.
- until 13:58:22: `https://registry.npmjs.org/@activepieces/piece-microsoft-365-planner/-/piece-microsoft-365-planner-0.4.0.tgz` returns `404 {"error":"Not found"}`; the dropdown (`POST /v1/pieces/options`) fails.
- from 13:58:22: the tarball returns 200 and the step works, with no restart or cache clear.

npm doesn't guarantee that a version is downloadable as soon as it's listed. Usually the gap is seconds; this one was about 4 minutes.

## Proposed fix

Gate each piece's metadata insert on its own tarball being downloadable:

- For each piece published in the run, send a `HEAD` request to its npm tarball URL (status only, no download) every 10 s until it returns 200.
- Check in parallel batches of about 20, the same batching `update-pieces-metadata.ts` already uses, so a bulk release takes about as long as its slowest tarball rather than the sum (around 15 s for 300 pieces when every tarball is ready).
- Insert each piece's metadata as soon as its own tarball returns 200, so one slow piece doesn't hold back the rest.
- If a piece's tarball still isn't ready after about 10 minutes, skip that piece's metadata, report it in the job log and the Discord failure notice, and let the other pieces go through.

Normally every tarball returns 200 on the first try, so this adds about a second per batch.
