issue.body:
Fixes [GIT-1989](https://linear.app/activepieces/issue/GIT-1989)
Closes #16343

## Problem
1. Failed row delete in the Tables editor: Alice disappears from the grid optimistically and Bob moves to row 0. The next edit of Bob is sent to Alice's record ID and overwrites Alice on the server.
2. Failed field delete: Email shifts to column 0, and the next Email edit is sent with the deleted Name field's ID.
3. Edits queued while the DELETE is still pending run after it rejects, with the same wrong IDs.

Cause: the client store removes rows and fields right away, but the server mirror in `ap-tables-server-state.ts` only removes them after the API call succeeds. The save queue kept running after a rejected write, so later writes looked up IDs by position in a stale mirror.

## Fix
- `ap-tables-server-state.ts`: the first failed write stops the table's save queue. Every queued and later write is skipped, `isSaving` resets, and `onSaveFailed(error)` fires. This is the single point all table writes go through, and the shared `PromiseQueue` is untouched.
- `ap-tables-client-state.tsx`: passes `onSaveFailed` through. `createApTableStore` and `createServerState` move to named object params (repo rule, and it stops two callback params from being swapped by accident).
- `ap-table-state-provider.tsx`: on failure, shows a "Your change was not saved" toast (the server's message when it has one) and rebuilds the store from freshly fetched table, fields and records through the existing `refreshTableState`. If that reload fails, the existing "Table not available" screen replaces the editor, so no further edits are accepted.
- One new en locale string.

## Verification
- New `failed-table-save.test.ts` (real client store, server mirror and queue, only the API mocked) plus 2 new provider tests. Red first: 4 of them fail on main and pass with the fix. The 2 success-path guards pass both ways.
- `test/features/tables`: 43/43 pass. `npm run lint-dev` clean. `tsc` on the web app shows no new errors.
- `/simplify`, `/code-review` and security review: done. Applied: show the server's error text in the toast, and named params. Left as known tradeoffs: see Non-happy scenarios.
- Real app (PGlite dev stack), DELETE forced to fail in the browser: a failed row delete and a failed field delete each send zero updates, including an edit made while the DELETE was pending. The toast appears and the table returns to server state. The inverse direction also works: after a successful row delete, the edit goes to Bob's ID, and after a successful field delete, it goes to the Email field ID.
- Visual: failed row delete (toast plus restored table), failed field delete (pending, then recovered), successful row delete. Before/after in the Visual verification comment.
- Other affected paths: checked. Every table write (record create, update and delete, field create, rename, reorder and delete, table rename and status) goes through the same `addPromiseToQueue`, so all are covered. Import writes in `table-hooks.ts` do not use the mirror. Left unfixed (it predates this PR and is unrelated): `serverState.records` keeps pointing at the first array after `deleteField`/`setRecords` reassign `clonedRecords`.
- Repro: browser XHR patch rejects only DELETE `/v1/records/` and `/v1/fields/`. On main, Alice's record is overwritten with "Robert" (full steps in the Reproduction block).
- Product decision embedded: a failed table save drops the unsaved queued edits and reloads the table from the server with a toast, the same as the flow builder's failed-save handling. Alternative considered: block the editor behind a "Reload table" button.

### Breaking change?

- [x] no, reviewed, not breaking
- [ ] yes, technical (removed/renamed API field or endpoint, dropped column, new required field, removed/required env var)
- [ ] yes, functional (default/limit/behaviour change, new self-hosted setup step)

### Security impact?

- [x] no, reviewed, no security impact
- [ ] yes, security-sensitive (call out the risk and mitigation in the description above)

<details>
<summary>Plan & reasoning</summary>

## Plan
- Halt at `addPromiseToQueue`, the one choke point every table write passes through.
- Recover by reusing the keyed remount (`refreshTableState`) that import and lock take-over already use, so both mirrors are rebuilt from the same server snapshot.
- Footprint estimate: 3 product files, about 20 lines, plus 1 locale key. Actual: 3 files, about 45 changed lines, plus 1 key. The growth over the estimate is the named-params conversion.

## Non-happy scenarios considered
- Edit queued while the DELETE is pending: skipped by the halted queue (unit test plus real app).
- Reload fails (offline): queries error out, the editor is replaced by the "Table not available" screen, and a later focus refetch builds a fresh store (provider test).
- DELETE applied on the server but the response was lost: the reload shows the true server state instead of guessing.
- Several failures in a row: only the first one fires the toast and reload. The toast has a fixed id, so toasts do not stack.
- Successful deletes: IDs still resolve correctly (unit tests plus real app).
- Transient error (one 502): saving still stops and the table reloads. Nothing is retried, unlike the builder's `sendWithRetries`. Sharing that retry code would be a cross-feature change, so it is left out.
- Edits made between the failure and the end of the reload (usually well under a second) are skipped and then replaced by server state. The toast that is already showing covers this.
- Reload fails: the existing "Table not available" screen is shown. Its wording suggests the table may be removed, but no edit can be applied against stale data.

## Alternatives rejected
- Halt inside the shared `PromiseQueue`: the flow builder uses it too (cross-feature).
- Blocking panel with a "Reload table" button (closed community PR #16344's shape): about 80 lines, 3 strings and new store state, and it does not match how the builder handles failed saves.
- Replaying or retrying the queued writes: they carry positions from the optimistic view, so replaying them is the bug.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Reproduction</summary>

## Environment
- `npm run dev` on main and on this branch: PGlite, in-memory queue, dev user `dev@ap.com`.
- Table "People" with text fields Name and Email. Records: Alice / alice@example.com, then Bob / bob@example.com.

## Harness
Paste in the browser console on the table page. It rejects only table DELETE requests, with a network error after `window.__failDelay` ms (default 300), and logs every request to `window.__reqs`:

```js
(() => {
  window.__reqs = [];
  const open = XMLHttpRequest.prototype.open;
  const send = XMLHttpRequest.prototype.send;
  XMLHttpRequest.prototype.open = function (method, url, ...rest) {
    this.__m = method; this.__u = String(url);
    window.__reqs.push(method + ' ' + String(url));
    return open.call(this, method, url, ...rest);
  };
  XMLHttpRequest.prototype.send = function (...args) {
    if (this.__m.toUpperCase() === 'DELETE' && /\/v1\/(records\/|fields\/)/.test(this.__u)) {
      window.__reqs.push('FAILED ' + this.__m + ' ' + this.__u);
      setTimeout(() => this.dispatchEvent(new ProgressEvent('error')), window.__failDelay || 300);
      Object.defineProperty(this, 'readyState', { value: 4 });
      return;
    }
    return send.apply(this, args);
  };
})()
```

## Trigger
- Rows: select Alice, Delete Records, Delete. Then edit the Name cell in row 1 (Bob) to "Robert".
- Fields: Name column menu, Delete, Delete. Then edit row 1's first visible cell (Email).
- Pending variant: set `window.__failDelay = 4000` and make the edit before the DELETE rejects.

## Results
| Run | Requests after the failed DELETE | Server state after reload |
| -- | -- | -- |
| main, row | `POST /v1/records/<alice-id>` | Alice's Name is "Robert", Bob unchanged |
| fix, row | none (table refetch only) | Alice and Bob unchanged, toast shown |
| fix, row, edit while pending | none | unchanged |
| fix, field, edit while pending | none | unchanged, Name column back |
| fix, successful row delete | `POST /v1/records/<bob-id>` | correct |
| fix, successful field delete | `POST /v1/records/<bob-id>` with the Email field ID | correct |
</details>

## Visual verification

Real app (`npm run dev`, PGlite), table "People" with Alice and Bob. The table DELETE request was made to fail in the browser, and every other request was left alone.

| Before (main) | After (this PR) |
| -- | -- |
| Failed delete of Alice, then edit Bob to "Robert": the grid looks right... ![before-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/majewskibartosz/activepieces/assets/git-1989-visual/before-1-local-view.png) | Failed delete of Alice: toast, and the table goes back to server state. No update request is sent. ![after-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/majewskibartosz/activepieces/assets/git-1989-visual/after-1-row-delete-failed.png) |
| ...but after a reload, Alice's record has become "Robert" (the edit went to Alice's ID) ![before-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/majewskibartosz/activepieces/assets/git-1989-visual/before-2-alice-overwritten.png) | Failed delete of Name, with an Email edit made while the DELETE was pending (no update sent) ![after-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/majewskibartosz/activepieces/assets/git-1989-visual/after-2-field-delete-pending.png) |
| | ...then the toast appears and the Name column is back ![after-3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/majewskibartosz/activepieces/assets/git-1989-visual/after-3-field-delete-failed.png) |

Driven states: failed row delete, failed field delete with an edit queued while pending, edit after recovery (goes to Bob's ID), successful row delete, successful field delete (edit sent with the Email field ID). Light theme only, because the toast is the existing sonner error toast.
